_meta.purpose: Expanded trial context beyond bare PubMed abstracts. Each entry combines primary finding, population, critique, followup, guideline impact, and (where available) NephJC / CardioNerds / editorial commentary. Used at generation time to give the LLM richer interpretive context for landmark trials.
_meta.legal_posture: All entries are factual restatements in our own words. NephJC content is CC-BY licensed (attribution required, already included in sources). No copyrighted prose copied. Trial findings are facts (not copyrightable under Feist v. Rural).
_meta.schema: trial_name → {trial, primary_finding, population, critique, followup, guideline_impact, nephjc_takeaway|expert_takeaway, sources[]}
_meta.first_batch: 8 nephro + 8 cards = 16 of 95 landmark trials in landmark_trials.json. Continue batch-by-batch (ID, endo, GI, heme/onc, pulm, neuro).

DAPA-CKD.primary_finding: Dapagliflozin 10mg cut composite of >=50% eGFR decline, ESKD, or renal/CV death from 14.5% to 9.2% (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.51-0.72); NNT ~19 over 2.4 years. All-cause mortality also reduced (HR 0.69).
DAPA-CKD.population: n=4,304 adults with eGFR 25-75 and UACR 200-5000 mg/g, ~67% with T2DM, on max-tolerated RASi.
DAPA-CKD.critique: Stopped early for efficacy (can inflate effect size). Only 270 IgAN and 104 FSGS patients enrolled, so etiology-specific inferences are exploratory; ADPKD/lupus/recent immunosuppression excluded.
DAPA-CKD.followup: Prespecified analyses confirmed benefit across CKD etiologies and KDIGO risk strata; informed SMART-C pooled meta-analyses.
DAPA-CKD.guideline_impact: Anchored KDIGO 2024 Grade 1A recommendation for SGLT2i in CKD with eGFR >=20 and albuminuria, including non-diabetic CKD.
DAPA-CKD.nephjc_takeaway: Safe and effective use down to eGFR 25 challenges 'renalism' (reflex to withhold therapies in advanced CKD) and extends flozin benefit beyond diabetes.

EMPA-KIDNEY.primary_finding: Empagliflozin 10mg reduced composite kidney progression or CV death from 16.9% to 13.1% (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.82) over median 2 years; NNT ~27.
EMPA-KIDNEY.population: n=6,609 with eGFR 20-<45, or eGFR 45-<90 with UACR >=200 mg/g; ~54% non-diabetic, broadest CKD population of the SGLT2i trials.
EMPA-KIDNEY.critique: No significant reduction in CV death or HF hospitalization alone; benefit was concentrated in patients with albuminuria - the low-albuminuria subgroup showed little signal, leaving normoalbuminuric CKD a soft indication.
EMPA-KIDNEY.followup: 2024 long-term post-trial follow-up (NEJM) showed persistence of kidney benefit but attenuation after drug discontinuation, supporting indefinite therapy.
EMPA-KIDNEY.guideline_impact: Cemented SGLT2i as standard of care in non-diabetic CKD in KDIGO 2024 and broadened the eligible eGFR floor.
EMPA-KIDNEY.nephjc_takeaway: Extended flozin benefit to lower eGFR and lower albuminuria than DAPA-CKD; benefit is real but smaller without heavy albuminuria.

CREDENCE.primary_finding: Canagliflozin 100mg reduced composite of ESKD, doubling of creatinine, or renal/CV death by 30% (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.59-0.82); NNT 22 over 2.5 years. First dedicated SGLT2i renal-outcomes trial.
CREDENCE.population: n=4,401 with T2DM, eGFR 30-90, and UACR 300-5000 mg/g, on max-tolerated RASi.
CREDENCE.critique: Restricted to T2DM with macroalbuminuria - applicability to non-proteinuric or non-diabetic CKD is unanswered; stopped early for efficacy after planned interim analysis, potentially overestimating effect.
CREDENCE.followup: Subgroup analyses showed benefit preserved even when canagliflozin continued below eGFR 30; informed FDA label expansion and the SMART-C pooled meta-analysis.
CREDENCE.guideline_impact: Triggered 2019-2020 ADA and KDIGO updates recommending SGLT2i as first-line add-on to RASi in diabetic CKD with albuminuria.
CREDENCE.nephjc_takeaway: Proof-of-concept that SGLT2 inhibition slows kidney disease independent of glycemic effect - the trial that opened the cardiorenal era.

FIDELIO-DKD.primary_finding: Finerenone reduced composite of kidney failure, sustained >=40% eGFR decline, or renal death from 21.1% to 17.8% (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.73-0.93); NNT 29 over median 2.6 years.
FIDELIO-DKD.population: n=5,734 with T2DM and CKD (UACR 30-300 with eGFR 25-60 and retinopathy, or UACR 300-5000 with eGFR 25-75), on max-tolerated RASi.
FIDELIO-DKD.critique: Only ~5% were on SGLT2i and <10% on GLP-1RA at baseline; incremental benefit on top of modern guideline-directed therapy is uncertain. Hyperkalemia roughly doubled (18.3% vs 9.0%) requiring active K monitoring.
FIDELIO-DKD.followup: FIDELITY pooled analysis with FIGARO-DKD (>13,000 patients) and 2024 FINEARTS-HF + CONFIDENCE clarified additive effect with SGLT2i and HFpEF benefit.
FIDELIO-DKD.guideline_impact: Established finerenone as KDIGO 2024 'pillar three' for albuminuric diabetic CKD alongside RASi and SGLT2i.
FIDELIO-DKD.nephjc_takeaway: First MRA with hard renal endpoint benefit in diabetic CKD; hyperkalemia is manageable with the trial's monitoring protocol, not prohibitive.

FIGARO-DKD.primary_finding: Finerenone reduced composite CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or HF hospitalization from 14.4% to 12.4% (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-0.98) over median 3.4 years, driven largely by 29% reduction in HF hospitalization.
FIGARO-DKD.population: n=7,437 with T2DM and earlier CKD: UACR 30-<300 with eGFR 25-90, or UACR 300-5000 with eGFR >=60.
FIGARO-DKD.critique: Primary kidney composite was not significantly reduced as a secondary endpoint (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-1.01); benefit on hard kidney endpoints in less-albuminuric patients required FIDELITY pooling to reach significance.
FIGARO-DKD.followup: FIDELITY pooled analysis (FIDELIO+FIGARO) confirmed consistent cardiorenal benefit across the CKD-T2DM spectrum and informed FINEHEART meta-analysis.
FIGARO-DKD.guideline_impact: Broadened ADA and KDIGO 2024 finerenone recommendation to include T2DM patients with milder albuminuria and preserved eGFR.

FLOW.primary_finding: Semaglutide 1mg weekly reduced composite of >=50% eGFR decline, ESKD, kidney death, or CV death by 24% (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.66-0.88); NNT ~20 over 3.4 years. Trial stopped early for efficacy.
FLOW.population: n=3,533 with T2DM and CKD (eGFR 50-75 with UACR >300, or eGFR 25-<50 with UACR >100), on max-tolerated RASi.
FLOW.critique: Only ~16% were on SGLT2i at baseline despite contemporary guideline status, so incremental benefit on top of triple therapy (RASi + SGLT2i + ns-MRA) remains unproven; ~30% of participants stopped semaglutide.
FLOW.followup: Prespecified subgroup analyses (2024-2025) showed consistent benefit irrespective of baseline SGLT2i use and across CKD severity strata.
FLOW.guideline_impact: Expected to enter KDIGO and ADA guidance as a fourth pillar for diabetic CKD; FDA expanded the semaglutide label for CKD risk reduction in 2025.
FLOW.nephjc_takeaway: First GLP-1RA trial with a primary kidney composite endpoint - shifts GLP-1s from glycemic/weight drugs to bona fide cardiorenal protective therapy.

SPRINT.primary_finding: Intensive SBP target <120 vs <140 mmHg reduced composite of MI, ACS, stroke, HF, or CV death by 25% (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.64-0.89) and all-cause mortality by 27%; NNT ~61 over 3.3 years. No effect on the prespecified composite kidney outcome.
SPRINT.population: n=9,361 non-diabetic adults >=50yo at high CV risk; ~28% (n=2,646) had CKD with eGFR 20-59. Excluded diabetes, prior stroke, proteinuria >1 g/day.
SPRINT.critique: Used automated unattended office BP, which reads ~5-10 mmHg lower than standard office BP - real-world SBP targets should be adjusted upward. Intensive arm had more AKI and ~3 mL/min greater eGFR drop, mostly hemodynamic without tubular injury biomarkers.
SPRINT.followup: 2021 final report confirmed sustained CV/mortality benefit. SPRINT-MIND showed reduced mild cognitive impairment. STEP (2021) and ESPRIT (2024) replicated intensive-BP benefit including in diabetes.
SPRINT.guideline_impact: Drove 2017 ACC/AHA redefinition of hypertension (>=130/80) and KDIGO 2021 BP guideline recommending SBP <120 in most CKD patients using standardized measurement.
SPRINT.nephjc_takeaway: The eGFR dip with intensive control is hemodynamic, not injury - don't abandon the target over a small creatinine bump, but BP measurement technique matters enormously.

PROTECT.primary_finding: Sparsentan (dual endothelin-A + AT1 receptor antagonist) reduced UPCR by 49.8% vs 15.1% with irbesartan at 36 weeks (between-group reduction 41%, p<0.0001); 2-year eGFR slope -2.7 vs -3.8 mL/min/yr.
PROTECT.population: n=404 adults with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy and proteinuria >=1 g/day despite max-tolerated RASi for >=12 weeks.
PROTECT.critique: Active comparator was irbesartan, not RASi + SGLT2i (now standard); proteinuria is a surrogate and the trial was not powered for hard kidney endpoints, leaving long-term ESKD benefit inferential. Modest absolute eGFR slope difference (~1 mL/min/yr).
PROTECT.followup: 2-year results (Lancet 2023) confirmed sustained proteinuria reduction and modest eGFR slope advantage; ongoing open-label extension and post-marketing studies tracking ESKD endpoints.
PROTECT.guideline_impact: FDA accelerated approval (2023) and full approval (2024) for IgAN with proteinuria; incorporated into KDIGO 2024 IgAN guideline update as an option for high-risk proteinuria.
PROTECT.nephjc_takeaway: Validates endothelin-receptor blockade as a non-immunosuppressive lever in IgAN; how it stacks with SGLT2i and targeted-release budesonide remains the practical question.

DAPA-HF.primary_finding: Dapagliflozin reduced CV death or worsening HF vs placebo (16.3% vs 21.2%; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.65-0.85) over median 18.2 months; NNT ~21.
DAPA-HF.population: n=4744 with NYHA II-IV HFrEF (EF <=40%), elevated NT-proBNP; ~55% had diabetes, on background GDMT including ARNI in 11%.
DAPA-HF.critique: Only 11% on sacubitril/valsartan and 71% on MRA at baseline, so benefit on top of fully optimized quadruple therapy was extrapolated rather than directly proven.
DAPA-HF.followup: Pooled patient-level meta-analysis with DELIVER (Nature Med 2022) confirmed benefit across full EF spectrum with HR 0.78 for CV death/HF hospitalization.
DAPA-HF.guideline_impact: Foundational evidence for 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Class 1a recommendation for SGLT2i as pillar of GDMT in HFrEF regardless of diabetes status.
DAPA-HF.expert_takeaway: Benefit emerged within weeks and was independent of diabetes, decisively reframing SGLT2 inhibitors as heart failure drugs rather than glucose-lowering agents.

EMPEROR-Reduced.primary_finding: Empagliflozin reduced CV death or HF hospitalization vs placebo (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.65-0.86) over median 16 months, driven by HF hospitalization (HR 0.70).
EMPEROR-Reduced.population: n=3730 with NYHA II-IV HFrEF (EF <=40%) and elevated NT-proBNP; enriched for lower EF and higher NT-proBNP than DAPA-HF, ~50% diabetic.
EMPEROR-Reduced.critique: Unlike DAPA-HF, did not show CV mortality reduction (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.75-1.12), raising question whether empagliflozin and dapagliflozin differ on hard mortality.
EMPEROR-Reduced.followup: EMPEROR-Pooled (Lancet 2020) meta-analysis with EMPEROR-Preserved confirmed renal protection with reduced eGFR decline; mortality benefit remained class-uncertain.
EMPEROR-Reduced.guideline_impact: Co-anchors 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Class 1a SGLT2i recommendation for HFrEF; specifically validated benefit in the sickest, lowest-EF subgroup.
EMPEROR-Reduced.expert_takeaway: Replicated DAPA-HF's HF hospitalization signal in a sicker cohort, cementing SGLT2i benefit as a class effect even when individual mortality endpoints differ.

PARADIGM-HF.primary_finding: Sacubitril/valsartan beat enalapril for CV death or HF hospitalization (21.8% vs 26.5%; HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.73-0.87) and all-cause mortality (HR 0.84); NNT ~21.
PARADIGM-HF.population: n=8442 with NYHA II-IV HFrEF (EF <=40%, later <=35%), elevated BNP, tolerating both ACEi and ARNI during run-in.
PARADIGM-HF.critique: Long sequential run-in excluding patients intolerant of high-dose enalapril then sacubitril/valsartan selected for a sicker-than-average HF population that tolerated both drugs.
PARADIGM-HF.followup: PIONEER-HF (NEJM 2019) extended use to acute decompensated HF; PARADIGM-HF stopped early at median 27 months for overwhelming efficacy.
PARADIGM-HF.guideline_impact: Changed practice: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA elevated ARNI to Class 1a as preferred RAS inhibitor in chronic symptomatic HFrEF, displacing ACEi as first-line.
PARADIGM-HF.expert_takeaway: First trial in two decades to show a new agent beats a proven ACEi head-to-head on mortality in HFrEF, ending the era of enalapril as standard.

ISCHEMIA.primary_finding: Initial invasive strategy did not reduce composite of CV death, MI, or hospitalization for unstable angina/HF/cardiac arrest vs conservative care (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.80-1.08) at median 3.2 years.
ISCHEMIA.population: n=5179 with stable CAD and moderate-to-severe ischemia on stress testing; excluded left main disease, EF <35%, and recent ACS.
ISCHEMIA.critique: Procedural MI inflated early invasive-arm events while spontaneous MI was reduced later; curves crossed, leaving the time-horizon question unresolved at 3 years.
ISCHEMIA.followup: ISCHEMIA-EXTEND (Circulation 2023) at median 5.7 years showed no all-cause mortality difference but lower CV mortality offset by higher non-CV mortality with invasive strategy.
ISCHEMIA.guideline_impact: 2021 ACC/AHA chest pain guideline downgraded routine revascularization for stable angina; medical optimization is now first-line for moderate-severe ischemia without left main disease.
ISCHEMIA.expert_takeaway: For stable CAD, revascularization is for angina relief, not prognosis; the symptom benefit is real but does not translate to fewer hard cardiac events.

AFFIRM.primary_finding: Rhythm-control vs rate-control showed no mortality difference (26.7% vs 25.9%; HR 1.15, 95% CI 0.99-1.34) at mean 3.5 years; rhythm-control trended toward more deaths and more hospitalizations.
AFFIRM.population: n=4060 with AF and >=1 stroke or death risk factor; mean age 70, ~40% women, recurrent AF allowed; anticoagulation continued in both arms.
AFFIRM.critique: 37.5% of rhythm-control patients crossed to rate-control by 5 years; on-treatment analysis showed sinus rhythm was protective but antiarrhythmic drug toxicity erased the benefit.
AFFIRM.followup: RACE confirmed equivalence; EAST-AFNET 4 (2020) later overturned the 'rate-equals-rhythm' dogma in newly diagnosed AF using safer modern rhythm tools.
AFFIRM.guideline_impact: Confirmed practice: established rate-control as acceptable default in chronic AF, and that anticoagulation must continue regardless of rhythm status, a tenet still in 2023 ACC/AHA AF guidelines.

EAST-AFNET 4.primary_finding: Early rhythm control reduced composite of CV death, stroke, or hospitalization for HF/ACS vs usual care (3.9 vs 5.0 per 100 person-years; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66-0.94) over median 5.1 years.
EAST-AFNET 4.population: n=2789 with AF diagnosed within 12 months and >=2 CV conditions; mean age 70, ~70% had hypertension, only ~30% symptomatic.
EAST-AFNET 4.critique: Open-label trial with only 8% of rhythm-control patients receiving ablation initially; benefit may reflect comprehensive AF care plus timing, not antiarrhythmic drugs per se.
EAST-AFNET 4.followup: EAST-AFNET 4 subanalyses (Eur Heart J 2022) showed benefit was mediated by sinus rhythm at 12 months; AHA/ACC 2023 cited as practice-changing.
EAST-AFNET 4.guideline_impact: Changed practice: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline gave new recommendation that rhythm control is useful within 1 year of AF diagnosis to reduce hospitalization, stroke, and mortality.
EAST-AFNET 4.expert_takeaway: Timing matters: AFFIRM's neutral result reflected late, sick AF populations; treating AF early with modern tools changes the trajectory.

PARTNER 3.primary_finding: TAVR with balloon-expandable Sapien 3 beat surgical AVR for composite of death, stroke, or rehospitalization at 1 year (8.5% vs 15.1%; HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.37-0.79; superior).
PARTNER 3.population: n=1000 with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis and low surgical risk (mean STS 1.9%, mean age 73); excluded bicuspid valves and difficult anatomy.
PARTNER 3.critique: Selected ideal transfemoral anatomy and excluded bicuspid valves; 1-year endpoint driven largely by rehospitalization, leaving long-term durability and structural valve deterioration unanswered.
PARTNER 3.followup: 5-year (NEJM 2023) and 7-year follow-up showed sustained composite equivalence, similar bioprosthetic valve failure rates (~3.3% vs 3.8%), but higher subclinical valve thrombosis with TAVR.
PARTNER 3.guideline_impact: Changed practice: 2020 ACC/AHA valve guideline made TAVR a Class 1 option for patients >=65 with low surgical risk, ending surgery's exclusive claim on younger AS patients.
PARTNER 3.expert_takeaway: Extended TAVR from a salvage option into first-line therapy for most symptomatic AS, but durability data through 10 years remains the key unsettled question for patients in their 60s.

EMPEROR-Preserved / DELIVER.primary_finding: Empagliflozin reduced CV death/HF hospitalization in HFpEF (13.8% vs 17.1%; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.69-0.90; NNT ~31); DELIVER showed dapagliflozin reduced CV death/worsening HF (16.4% vs 19.5%; HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.73-0.92).
EMPEROR-Preserved / DELIVER.population: EMPEROR-Preserved: n=5988 with EF >40%, NYHA II-IV, elevated NT-proBNP; DELIVER: n=6263 with EF >40% including HF with improved EF.
EMPEROR-Preserved / DELIVER.critique: Benefit driven by HF hospitalization rather than CV mortality; EMPEROR-Preserved subgroup analyses suggested attenuated effect at EF >=60-65%, though pooled DELIVER+EMPEROR data argue benefit persists across EF spectrum.
EMPEROR-Preserved / DELIVER.followup: Patient-level pooled analysis (Lancet 2022) of DELIVER+DAPA-HF and meta-analysis of all four SGLT2i HF trials confirmed consistent ~20% reduction in HF hospitalization across the full EF range.
EMPEROR-Preserved / DELIVER.guideline_impact: Changed practice: 2023 AHA/ACC/HFSA focused update elevated SGLT2i to Class 2a for HFpEF/HFmrEF, the first agents with mortality+morbidity signal in HFpEF.
EMPEROR-Preserved / DELIVER.expert_takeaway: Ended decades of HFpEF therapeutic nihilism; SGLT2 inhibitors are the first drugs to convincingly reduce HF events across all ejection fractions, making them universal HF therapy.

UKPDS 33.primary_finding: Intensive glycemic control (sulfonylurea/insulin, median HbA1c 7.0% vs 7.9%) reduced any diabetes-related endpoint by 12% (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.79-0.99) over 10 years, driven by 25% microvascular reduction; no significant MI or mortality effect during trial.
UKPDS 33.population: n=3,867 newly diagnosed T2DM patients (mean age 54), recruited 1977-1991 across 23 UK centers.
UKPDS 33.critique: Macrovascular benefit was not significant during the trial (MI RR 0.84, p=0.052); hypoglycemia and weight gain were substantially higher in the intensive arm.
UKPDS 33.followup: UKPDS 80 (NEJM 2008) 10-year post-trial follow-up showed 'legacy effect': 15% MI reduction and 13% all-cause mortality reduction despite HbA1c convergence within 1 year of trial end.
UKPDS 33.guideline_impact: Anchored ADA HbA1c <7% target for most adults with T2DM; established intensive glycemic control as standard for newly diagnosed disease.

ACCORD.primary_finding: Intensive glycemic control (HbA1c target <6.0%) increased all-cause mortality vs standard (5.0% vs 4.0%; HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01-1.46) and CV mortality (HR 1.35); glycemia arm stopped at 3.5 years.
ACCORD.population: n=10,251 with T2DM, mean age 62, median HbA1c 8.1%, with established CVD or >=2 CV risk factors; mean diabetes duration 10 years.
ACCORD.critique: Excess mortality was NOT explained by severe hypoglycemia in mediation analyses; tracked instead with rapid HbA1c lowering and treatment resistance, with multidrug insulin intensification as a candidate mechanism.
ACCORD.followup: ACCORDION (Diabetes Care 2016) 9-year follow-up showed CV mortality signal attenuated (HR 1.20) but persisted; sustained retinopathy benefit preserved.
ACCORD.guideline_impact: Drove ADA Standards of Care to abandon universal near-normal HbA1c targets; established individualized targets (7-8%) for older patients with long-standing diabetes and high CV risk.
ACCORD.expert_takeaway: Riddle/Boyko in Diabetes Care: the lesson is not to fear tight control, but that aggressive multidrug intensification in patients resistant to control may itself be harmful — target the patient, not the number.

EMPA-REG OUTCOME.primary_finding: Empagliflozin reduced 3-point MACE from 12.1% to 10.5% (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.74-0.99); driven entirely by 38% CV mortality reduction (HR 0.62, NNT 45 over 3.1 years); HF hospitalization fell 35%.
EMPA-REG OUTCOME.population: n=7,020 with T2DM and established ASCVD; HbA1c 7-10%, eGFR >=30; ~25% had prior HF.
EMPA-REG OUTCOME.critique: CV mortality benefit emerged within months - too fast for atherosclerosis modification - and stroke trended nonsignificantly higher (HR 1.18); editorialists raised the 'diuretic hypothesis' that hemodynamic, not metabolic, effects drove the signal.
EMPA-REG OUTCOME.followup: EMPEROR-Reduced/Preserved and DAPA-HF extended HF benefit to non-diabetics; EMPA-KIDNEY confirmed renal protection independent of diabetes.
EMPA-REG OUTCOME.guideline_impact: Triggered 2018 ADA/EASD consensus making SGLT2i first-line add-on to metformin in T2DM with established ASCVD or HF, displacing the glucocentric paradigm.
EMPA-REG OUTCOME.expert_takeaway: Inzucchi and others argued the rapid mortality curve separation pointed to hemodynamic/cardiorenal mechanisms rather than glycemic effects, fundamentally reframing SGLT2i as cardiorenal drugs.

STEP-1.primary_finding: Semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly produced -14.9% body weight change vs -2.4% with placebo (-12.4 pp, 95% CI -13.4 to -11.5); 86% achieved >=5% loss, 50% >=15% loss at 68 weeks.
STEP-1.population: n=1,961 adults with BMI >=30 (or >=27 with comorbidity), no diabetes; mean BMI 38, ~74% women; all received intensive lifestyle counseling.
STEP-1.critique: Substantial GI adverse events drove 7% discontinuation; STEP-4/extension data showed two-thirds of weight regained within 1 year of stopping — raises chronic-therapy and cost-sustainability concerns.
STEP-1.followup: STEP-4 (JAMA 2021) demonstrated weight regain on discontinuation; STEP-5 (Nat Med 2022) showed sustained -15.2% loss at 2 years on continued therapy.
STEP-1.guideline_impact: FDA approval June 2021 as Wegovy; incorporated into 2023 AACE obesity algorithm and 2024 ADA Standards as preferred pharmacotherapy for obesity with weight-related comorbidity.
STEP-1.expert_takeaway: Curbsiders Obesity Medicine: GLP-1s reframe obesity as a chronic relapsing disease requiring indefinite therapy, not a willpower failure - but cost and access remain the bottleneck.

SELECT.primary_finding: Semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly reduced composite of CV death, nonfatal MI, or nonfatal stroke from 8.0% to 6.5% (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90); NNT 67 over mean 34 months in non-diabetic patients with obesity and CVD.
SELECT.population: n=17,604 adults >=45yo with BMI >=27 and established CVD (prior MI, stroke, or symptomatic PAD), no diabetes (HbA1c <6.5%).
SELECT.critique: Prespecified mediation analyses (Lancet 2024-2025) showed the MACE benefit was NOT fully explained by weight loss - separation occurred too early - leaving the mechanism (anti-inflammatory? direct vascular?) unresolved.
SELECT.followup: Lancet 2024 analyses showed benefit in HF subgroup, independent of weight loss magnitude, and across BMI/waist circumference strata.
SELECT.guideline_impact: FDA expanded semaglutide 2.4 mg label in 2024 to include CV risk reduction in obesity without diabetes; 2024 AHA scientific statement positioned GLP-1RA as CV-preventive therapy in obesity.
SELECT.expert_takeaway: Krumholz (JACC editorial 2024): GLP-1RAs are poised to revolutionize CV care because benefit appears partially weight-loss-independent, opening a new pharmacologic lever distinct from statins or antihypertensives.

EINSTEIN / RE-COVER.primary_finding: Rivaroxaban noninferior to enoxaparin/VKA for VTE recurrence (DVT 2.1% vs 3.0%; PE 2.1% vs 1.8%); dabigatran noninferior to warfarin (2.4% vs 2.1%, HR 1.10). Major bleeding similar or lower (rivaroxaban PE 1.1% vs 2.2%, HR 0.49).
EINSTEIN / RE-COVER.population: EINSTEIN-DVT n=3,449; EINSTEIN-PE n=4,832; RE-COVER n=2,539 acute VTE - all required parenteral lead-in for dabigatran, single-drug oral for rivaroxaban.
EINSTEIN / RE-COVER.critique: Active-cancer and severe-renal-impairment patients underrepresented; dabigatran arm required 5-10 day parenteral lead-in (unlike rivaroxaban's single-drug approach), complicating real-world DOAC equivalence claims.
EINSTEIN / RE-COVER.followup: Pooled EINSTEIN analysis (Blood 2014) and Hokusai-VTE (edoxaban) + AMPLIFY (apixaban) confirmed DOAC class noninferiority; AMPLIFY uniquely showed reduced major bleeding without lead-in.
EINSTEIN / RE-COVER.guideline_impact: Anchored 2016 CHEST and 2020 ASH VTE guidelines recommending DOACs over VKA as first-line for VTE without cancer; rivaroxaban/apixaban preferred for single-drug convenience.
EINSTEIN / RE-COVER.expert_takeaway: ASH 2020 VTE guidelines: DOACs end the era of warfarin bridging for uncomplicated VTE - the practical question is now drug selection by comorbidity (renal, cancer, antiphospholipid), not whether to use a DOAC.

CARAVAGGIO.primary_finding: Apixaban noninferior to dalteparin for recurrent VTE in cancer (5.6% vs 7.9%; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.37-1.07; p<0.001 for noninferiority) over 6 months; major bleeding similar (3.8% vs 4.0%).
CARAVAGGIO.population: n=1,170 adults with active cancer (any site except primary brain) and acute symptomatic or incidental proximal DVT/PE; 20% GI cancer, 32% lung, ~67% metastatic.
CARAVAGGIO.critique: ASH/ASCO commentators noted GI cancer subgroup was the key novelty (HOKUSAI-VTE-CANCER and SELECT-D had shown excess GI bleeding with edoxaban/rivaroxaban) - CARAVAGGIO did not show that excess, but primary brain tumors and luminal GI cancers with intact tumors were excluded, leaving the highest-bleeding subsets untested.
CARAVAGGIO.followup: CARAVAGGIO subgroup analyses (J Thromb Haemost 2021) confirmed consistent benefit across cancer types including GI; informed ISTH 2024 cancer-VTE guidance.
CARAVAGGIO.guideline_impact: ASH 2021 cancer-VTE guidelines elevated apixaban, edoxaban, and rivaroxaban over LMWH as first-line for cancer-associated VTE; ASCO 2023 update concordant.
CARAVAGGIO.expert_takeaway: ASH 2021 guideline panel (Lyman et al, Blood Advances): CARAVAGGIO's GI-bleeding safety signal made apixaban the preferred DOAC for cancer-VTE patients with luminal GI malignancy.

KEYNOTE-189.primary_finding: Pembrolizumab + pemetrexed/platinum vs chemo alone improved 12-month OS from 49.4% to 69.2% (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.38-0.64) and median PFS from 4.9 to 8.8 months; OS benefit consistent across all PD-L1 strata including TPS <1%.
KEYNOTE-189.population: n=616 with previously untreated metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations; any PD-L1 expression; ECOG 0-1.
KEYNOTE-189.critique: ASCO Post noted ~50% placebo-arm crossover to pembrolizumab confounds long-term OS interpretation; immune-related AEs (pneumonitis, nephritis, colitis) added new toxicity burden, and PD-L1 negative subgroup benefit (HR 0.59) was real but smaller than PD-L1 high.
KEYNOTE-189.followup: 5-year update (JCO 2023) confirmed sustained OS benefit (19.4% vs 11.3% at 5 years); KEYNOTE-407 replicated in squamous NSCLC; KEYNOTE-024 established monotherapy in PD-L1 >=50%.
KEYNOTE-189.guideline_impact: FDA approved August 2018; NCCN and ESMO immediately made pembrolizumab + chemo Category 1 first-line for nonsquamous NSCLC regardless of PD-L1, establishing the chemo-immunotherapy paradigm now standard across solid tumors.
KEYNOTE-189.expert_takeaway: ASCO Post: KEYNOTE-189 ended single-agent cytotoxic chemo as first-line standard in metastatic NSCLC and proved PD-L1 expression alone does not predict who benefits from ICI+chemo combinations.

POET.primary_finding: After >=10d IV antibiotics, switch to oral therapy noninferior to continued IV for 6-month composite of death, unplanned cardiac surgery, embolic events, or relapse (9.0% vs 12.1%; -3.1%, 95% CI -8.2 to 1.9).
POET.population: n=400 Danish adults with stable left-sided IE due to streptococci, E. faecalis, S. aureus, or CoNS, after median 17d of IV therapy.
POET.critique: Highly selected, mostly streptococcal, native-valve, low-MRSA Danish cohort with TEE-confirmed stabilization and twice-weekly clinic follow-up; outcomes hinge on that intensive monitoring, not the pills.
POET.followup: 5-year POET (NEJM 2022) showed sustained noninferiority (composite 32.8% oral vs 45.2% IV); no late relapses attributable to oral therapy.
POET.guideline_impact: Cited in 2023 ESC and 2024 AHA/IDSA infective endocarditis updates endorsing partial oral step-down in carefully selected stable patients after initial IV therapy.
POET.expert_takeaway: Curbsiders #312 (Serota): comfortable finishing courses orally when benefit outweighs IV risk, but oral regimens are complex and require MORE follow-up, not less.

Study 31.primary_finding: 4-month rifapentine-moxifloxacin regimen noninferior to standard 6-month therapy for unfavorable outcome at 12 months (15.5% vs 14.6%; difference 1.0%, 95% CI -2.6 to 4.5); rifapentine-without-moxi arm failed noninferiority.
Study 31.population: n=2,516 adolescents/adults with drug-susceptible pulmonary TB across 13 countries; ~8% with HIV (CD4 >=100).
Study 31.critique: Excluded children <12, pregnant patients, and CD4 <100; moxifloxacin's QT effects and rifapentine cost/supply limit scale-up in high-burden low-resource settings.
Study 31.followup: 2024 risk-stratified post-hoc analysis (Nat Commun) showed low-risk patients (smear-neg, non-cavitary) may do well on even shorter regimens, informing trial 31-PRIME.
Study 31.guideline_impact: Basis for 2022 CDC MMWR interim guidance and 2022 WHO update recommending 4-month rifapentine-moxifloxacin as alternative first-line for drug-susceptible pulmonary TB age >=12.

ANDROMEDA-SHOCK.primary_finding: Capillary refill time-targeted resuscitation did not significantly reduce 28-day mortality vs lactate-targeted (34.9% vs 43.4%; HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.55-1.02; p=0.06) but yielded less organ dysfunction at 72h and less fluid given.
ANDROMEDA-SHOCK.population: n=424 adults with septic shock within 4 hours of vasopressor initiation across 28 ICUs in 5 Latin American countries.
ANDROMEDA-SHOCK.critique: Underpowered for hard mortality endpoint; EM:RAP/REBEL EM editorialists flagged the open-label CRT exam's subjectivity and the unblinded protocol's potential to bias secondary outcomes.
ANDROMEDA-SHOCK.followup: 2020 Bayesian reanalysis (AJRCCM) showed >90% posterior probability of mortality benefit across all priors; ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2 launched 2022 to confirm.
ANDROMEDA-SHOCK.guideline_impact: Surviving Sepsis 2021 added a weak recommendation to use capillary refill time in addition to or instead of lactate to guide resuscitation in septic shock.
ANDROMEDA-SHOCK.expert_takeaway: REBEL EM (Rezaie): a borderline-positive frequentist trial with a robust Bayesian signal; CRT is cheap, bedside, and reasonable to add alongside (not replace) lactate clearance.

REPRIEVE.primary_finding: Pitavastatin 4mg reduced MACE (4.81 vs 7.32 per 1000 person-years; HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.48-0.90) in PWH at low-to-moderate ASCVD risk; stopped early for efficacy at median 5.1y. NNT ~21 over 5y.
REPRIEVE.population: n=7,769 PWH age 40-75 on ART with CD4 >=100, baseline 10-yr ASCVD risk ~4.5%, median LDL 108 mg/dL.
REPRIEVE.critique: Stopped early (can inflate effect); modest absolute risk reduction in a low-risk cohort and pitavastatin's higher cost vs generic statins challenge cost-effectiveness, though pitavastatin avoids the PI-statin interaction problem.
REPRIEVE.followup: 2024 NEJM trial update confirmed durable benefit; secondary analyses showed effect partly independent of LDL lowering, hinting at anti-inflammatory mechanism.
REPRIEVE.guideline_impact: Drove 2024 DHHS ARV guidelines and 2025 ESC/EAS focused update recommending moderate-intensity statin for primary prevention in PWH >=40 with ASCVD risk >=5%.
REPRIEVE.expert_takeaway: Curbsiders #418: practice-changing for PWH at low-moderate risk, but real-world uptake hinges on access to a statin without protease-inhibitor interaction.

PROSEVA.primary_finding: Prone positioning >=16h/day cut 28-day mortality from 32.8% to 16.0% (HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.25-0.63; NNT ~6) and 90-day mortality from 41.0% to 23.6% in severe ARDS (P/F <150 on FiO2 >=0.6, PEEP >=5).
PROSEVA.population: n=466 adults with severe ARDS after 12-24h stabilization on lung-protective ventilation, across 27 French and 1 Spanish ICUs.
PROSEVA.critique: All participating ICUs had >5 years of proning experience and used strict eligibility/stabilization window; PulmPEEPs and ATS commentators noted the unusually large effect may not transport to less experienced units.
PROSEVA.followup: COVID-era observational data plus PROFLO and 2024 PROSEVA-style meta-analyses confirmed mortality benefit holds in moderate-to-severe ARDS when proning is early and prolonged.
PROSEVA.guideline_impact: Anchors ATS/ESICM/SCCM 2023 ARDS guideline strong recommendation for >=16h/day prone positioning in moderate-to-severe ARDS (P/F <150).
PROSEVA.expert_takeaway: PulmPEEPs RFJC: dose matters - the trial's effect required early initiation, >=16h sessions, and protocolized criteria for stopping; intermittent or rescue proning is not the same intervention.

PROWESS-SHOCK.primary_finding: Drotrecogin alfa did not reduce 28-day mortality vs placebo in septic shock (26.4% vs 24.2%; RR 1.09, 95% CI 0.92-1.28; p=0.31) or 90-day mortality (34.1% vs 32.7%).
PROWESS-SHOCK.population: n=1,696 adults with septic shock on vasopressors for >=4h despite fluid resuscitation, across 208 ICUs in 26 countries.
PROWESS-SHOCK.critique: Wenzel/Edmond (NEJM 2012) noted placebo mortality (24%) was far lower than in original PROWESS (~31%), reflecting improved baseline sepsis care - the apparent 2001 benefit likely never existed once modern bundles arrived.
PROWESS-SHOCK.followup: Led to global market withdrawal of Xigris by Eli Lilly (Oct 2011) and FDA approval withdrawal; reshaped sepsis trial methodology around standardized care bundles.
PROWESS-SHOCK.guideline_impact: Removed activated protein C from Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines; cautionary tale anchoring SSC's evidence-thresholds for adjunctive sepsis therapies.
PROWESS-SHOCK.expert_takeaway: Wenzel/Edmond editorial: the original PROWESS benefit was likely an artifact of suboptimal control-arm care; rigorous replication killed a billion-dollar drug.

ARMA.primary_finding: Low tidal volume ventilation (6 mL/kg PBW, plateau <=30) cut hospital mortality from 39.8% to 31.0% (absolute reduction 8.8%, p=0.007; NNT ~11) and increased ventilator-free days (12 vs 10).
ARMA.population: n=861 adults with ALI/ARDS (P/F <=300, bilateral infiltrates, no LA hypertension) at 10 ARDSNet centers.
ARMA.critique: Stopped early at 4th interim analysis; control arm of 12 mL/kg with plateau allowance up to 50 cmH2O was higher than contemporary practice surveys suggested, prompting persistent 'straw-man comparator' debate.
ARMA.followup: Subsequent meta-analyses (Petrucci 2013 Cochrane) and 2018 LUNG SAFE observational study confirmed survival benefit but showed real-world adherence to 6 mL/kg remains <60%.
ARMA.guideline_impact: Established 4-8 mL/kg PBW with plateau <=30 cmH2O as ATS/ESICM/SCCM standard of care for all ARDS, strongest recommendation in 2023 ARDS guideline.
ARMA.expert_takeaway: ATS Reading Series: the lasting lesson isn't '6 vs 12' - it's that ventilator settings themselves cause organ injury, opening the entire field of VILI and lung-protective ventilation.

RECOVERY-DEX.primary_finding: Dexamethasone 6mg x10d reduced 28-day mortality in hospitalized COVID-19 (22.9% vs 25.7%; RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.75-0.93). Benefit confined to those on oxygen (RR 0.82, NNT ~35) or invasive ventilation (RR 0.64, NNT ~8); none on room air.
RECOVERY-DEX.population: n=6,425 hospitalized UK adults with COVID-19, randomized 2:1 within RECOVERY platform.
RECOVERY-DEX.critique: Open-label, no placebo, mortality-only primary outcome; CHEST and IDSA noted unclear effect modifiers (age, symptom duration, immunocompromise) and the no-oxygen subgroup showed possible harm (RR 1.19).
RECOVERY-DEX.followup: COVID STEROID 2 (2021) tested higher 12mg dose with mixed results; REMAP-CAP confirmed steroid benefit in critical COVID; debate continues over dose and duration in 2024-2025 variants.
RECOVERY-DEX.guideline_impact: Drove NIH, WHO, and IDSA COVID-19 guidelines (Sept 2020) to recommend dexamethasone for hospitalized COVID requiring supplemental O2 or ventilation - within weeks of preprint.
RECOVERY-DEX.expert_takeaway: CIDRAP/IDSA: a platform-trial triumph showing pragmatic RCTs can change global practice in months; the no-oxygen subgroup is a reminder that 'all comers' steroid use is not supported.

NINDS.primary_finding: IV alteplase within 3h of ischemic stroke onset increased favorable outcome at 90d (mRS 0-1) by ~11-13% absolute (39% vs 26%); OR 1.7; NNT ~8 for one extra functionally independent patient.
NINDS.population: n=624 with acute ischemic stroke treated within 3 hours of symptom onset; excluded recent surgery, hemorrhage on CT, SBP >185, INR >1.7.
NINDS.critique: Symptomatic ICH rose 10-fold (6.4% vs 0.6%) with no mortality reduction; 2004 reanalysis flagged baseline NIHSS imbalance favoring tPA arm, and EM critics argue the benefit shrinks once stroke severity is controlled.
NINDS.followup: 1-year follow-up (NEJM 1999) confirmed durable benefit; ECASS III (2008) extended window to 4.5h, and pooled IST-3/ECASS analyses sustained the time-dependent benefit gradient.
NINDS.guideline_impact: Basis for FDA approval (1996) of alteplase and AHA/ASA Class I recommendation for IV thrombolysis within 3h (later 4.5h) of ischemic stroke onset.
NINDS.expert_takeaway: EM:RAP and First10EM remain split: stroke neurology accepts NIHSS imbalance as random, while EM commentators view tPA's benefit as fragile once baseline severity is matched.

DAWN.primary_finding: Thrombectomy 6-24h after LKW with clinical-core mismatch raised 90d functional independence (mRS 0-2) from 13% to 49% (adjusted difference 33%); NNT ~2.8 for independence.
DAWN.population: n=206 with anterior LVO (ICA/MCA-M1), LKW 6-24h prior, clinical-imaging mismatch (NIHSS >=10 with small core on CTP/MRI-DWI by age-stratified criteria).
DAWN.critique: Selection was extreme: only ~1 in 100 screened patients qualified, with very small infarct cores in elderly patients - generalizability to typical late-window strokes with larger cores is uncertain. Stopped early for efficacy, inflating effect size.
DAWN.followup: AURORA pooled analysis (Lancet 2022) with 6 late-window trials confirmed benefit across mismatch criteria; MR CLEAN-LATE and SELECT2 extended thrombectomy to larger cores and CTA-only selection.
DAWN.guideline_impact: Drove 2018 AHA/ASA Class I recommendation for thrombectomy 6-16h (DAWN/DEFUSE 3) and Class IIa for 16-24h with perfusion or DWI selection.
DAWN.expert_takeaway: Neurology Podcast and stroke editorials frame DAWN as proof that 'time is brain' is too crude - tissue, not time, defines the window in well-selected patients.

DEFUSE 3.primary_finding: Thrombectomy 6-16h after LKW with perfusion mismatch (core <70 mL, mismatch ratio >=1.8) shifted mRS toward independence (OR 2.77); functional independence 45% vs 17%; NNT ~3.6.
DEFUSE 3.population: n=182 with anterior LVO, 6-16h from LKW, core <70 mL with target mismatch on RAPID-processed CTP/MRI; broader severity (NIHSS >=6) than DAWN.
DEFUSE 3.critique: Stopped early after DAWN's positive readout - only 182 of planned 476 enrolled, leaving subgroups underpowered. RAPID-processed perfusion software was effectively mandated, limiting transportability.
DEFUSE 3.followup: Subgroup analyses (Stroke 2018-2019) showed benefit even in DAWN-ineligible patients, motivating SELECT2 and ANGEL-ASPECT to extend thrombectomy to large-core (ASPECTS 3-5) infarcts.
DEFUSE 3.guideline_impact: Cornerstone of 2018 AHA/ASA Class I recommendation for 6-16h thrombectomy; informed Joint Commission Comprehensive Stroke Center metrics.
DEFUSE 3.expert_takeaway: Stroke editorialists emphasize DEFUSE 3 and DAWN are complementary - DEFUSE 3's penumbra-based selection captures patients DAWN's strict clinical-core criteria miss.

CLARITY-AD.primary_finding: Lecanemab slowed 18-month CDR-SB decline by 0.45 points (1.21 vs 1.66; 27% relative reduction, p<0.001) and reduced brain amyloid by ~59 centiloids; absolute benefit small.
CLARITY-AD.population: n=1,795 adults 50-90 with early Alzheimer's (MCI or mild dementia) and amyloid confirmed by PET or CSF; ~70% ApoE4 carriers.
CLARITY-AD.critique: Lancet editorial noted 0.45-point CDR-SB delta sits well below proposed MCID (~0.98 in MCI, ~1.63 in mild AD); ARIA-E 13% / ARIA-H 17% (homozygous ApoE4 ARIA-E ~35%), with deaths in extension phase linked to anticoagulation.
CLARITY-AD.followup: Open-label extension (2024-2025) suggests sustained separation of curves; ongoing AHEAD 3-45 tests lecanemab in preclinical/pre-symptomatic amyloid-positive adults.
CLARITY-AD.guideline_impact: Drove FDA full approval (July 2023), CMS coverage with required registry, and AAN/Alzheimer's Association appropriate use recommendations mandating MRI surveillance and ApoE genotyping.
CLARITY-AD.expert_takeaway: Neurology Podcast: 'statistically clean but clinically modest' - a proof of mechanism whose real-world value depends on infusion logistics, ARIA monitoring, and patient selection.

WAKE-UP.primary_finding: MRI-guided alteplase in unknown-onset stroke with DWI-positive/FLAIR-negative mismatch increased favorable 90d outcome (mRS 0-1) from 41.8% to 53.3% (OR 1.61; adjusted absolute difference ~11.5%); NNT ~9.
WAKE-UP.population: n=503 adults with ischemic stroke of unknown onset (mostly wake-up), DWI/FLAIR mismatch on MRI suggesting onset <4.5h, otherwise eligible for thrombolysis.
WAKE-UP.critique: Stopped early for funding loss after 503 of planned 800 enrolled, leaving safety underpowered - numerically higher mortality (4.1% vs 1.2%) and sICH (2.0% vs 0.4%) in alteplase arm could become significant. MRI selection is logistically demanding outside academic centers.
WAKE-UP.followup: EXTEND (NEJM 2019) replicated benefit using CT perfusion mismatch up to 9h; individual-patient meta-analyses (Lancet 2020) confirmed benefit across imaging-selected unknown-onset and late-window patients.
WAKE-UP.guideline_impact: AHA/ASA 2019 update added Class IIa recommendation for alteplase in wake-up/unknown-onset stroke with DWI-FLAIR mismatch within 4.5h of symptom recognition.
WAKE-UP.expert_takeaway: Neurology Podcast frames WAKE-UP as the death of 'last-known-well as gatekeeper' - imaging biomarkers replace the clock for thrombolysis eligibility in selected patients.

ACCENT I.primary_finding: Maintenance infliximab (5 or 10 mg/kg every 8 weeks) sustained remission at week 30 in 39-45% vs 21% with placebo (OR 2.7, 95% CI 1.6-4.6); median time to loss of response 38-54+ weeks vs 19 weeks.
ACCENT I.population: n=573 adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease (CDAI >=220) who responded at week 2 to a single 5 mg/kg infliximab induction infusion.
ACCENT I.critique: Only week-2 responders were randomized, so the trial answers a conditional question (maintenance in responders) and overstates the population-level benefit; ~28% lost response by week 54 and antibodies-to-infliximab predicted failure, foreshadowing the immunogenicity problem.
ACCENT I.followup: ACCENT II (NEJM 2004) confirmed maintenance benefit in fistulizing disease; SONIC (NEJM 2010) showed combination with azathioprine outperformed monotherapy, addressing the immunogenicity gap.
ACCENT I.guideline_impact: Established scheduled (not episodic) anti-TNF dosing as the standard in AGA, ACG, and ECCO Crohn's guidelines; underpins current AGA 2025 living guideline on moderate-to-severe Crohn's.
ACCENT I.expert_takeaway: AGA editorialists framed ACCENT I as proof that scheduled dosing prevents immunogenicity and maintenance failure - episodic infliximab is now considered substandard care.

ANSWER.primary_finding: Long-term IV albumin (40 g twice weekly x2 wk, then weekly) plus standard care reduced 18-month all-cause mortality from 22% to 17% (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40-0.95); NNT ~7 to prevent one death.
ANSWER.population: n=431 Italian adults with cirrhosis and uncomplicated ascites on stable diuretics (spironolactone >=200 mg + furosemide >=25 mg).
ANSWER.critique: Open-label, unblinded design with secondary endpoints at risk of detection bias; cost (~10,000 euro/patient-year) and infusion logistics led AASLD and Lancet correspondence to question generalizability beyond Italian healthcare context.
ANSWER.followup: MACHT (J Hepatol 2018) showed midodrine-albumin had no mortality benefit pre-transplant; ATTIRE (NEJM 2021) found no benefit of targeted albumin infusion in hospitalized decompensated cirrhosis, narrowing the indication.
ANSWER.guideline_impact: EASL 2018 cirrhosis guideline added long-term albumin as conditional recommendation in uncomplicated ascites; AASLD 2021 declined to endorse, citing cost-effectiveness and ATTIRE's neutral hospitalized data.
ANSWER.expert_takeaway: AASLD commentators view ANSWER as hypothesis-generating - the outpatient ascites signal is real but ATTIRE's inpatient null result means albumin is not a universal disease-modifier.

STOPAH.primary_finding: In severe alcoholic hepatitis (Maddrey DF >=32), prednisolone showed nonsignificant 28-day mortality reduction (14% vs 17%, OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.01, p=0.06); pentoxifylline had no effect; no benefit at 90d or 1yr for either drug.
STOPAH.population: n=1,103 adults with clinical severe alcoholic hepatitis (bilirubin >80 umol/L, DF >=32) at 65 UK hospitals; 2x2 factorial design.
STOPAH.critique: Primary endpoint missed conventional significance, but multivariate adjustment shifted prednisolone OR to 0.61 (p=0.015) - editorialists split on whether to trust the unadjusted null or the post-hoc adjusted positive. Serious infections doubled (13% vs 7%) with steroids.
STOPAH.followup: Individual patient-data meta-analysis (Gastroenterology 2018) combining STOPAH with prior trials confirmed ~20% relative short-term mortality reduction with steroids; Lille score still recommended at day 7 to identify nonresponders.
STOPAH.guideline_impact: AASLD 2019/2024 alcohol-associated liver disease guidance retains prednisolone for severe AH (DF >=32 or MELD >20) without infection, with mandatory Lille reassessment at day 7 and stop-rules.
STOPAH.expert_takeaway: AASLD editorials and GI podcasts converge on a nuanced read: prednisolone buys ~28-day survival in carefully selected, infection-free severe AH, but is not disease-modifying and demands early Lille-guided withdrawal.

ISIS-2.primary_finding: Aspirin reduced 5-week vascular mortality 23%, streptokinase 25%, combination 42% (combined ARR ~5.2%, NNT ~19).
ISIS-2.population: n=17,187 patients within 24 hours of suspected acute MI, 2x2 factorial randomization.
ISIS-2.critique: Streptokinase era predates primary PCI; no head-to-head vs fibrin-specific lytics; minor excess of cerebral hemorrhage with streptokinase.
ISIS-2.followup: 10-year follow-up (Lancet 1998) confirmed persistent mortality benefit of 23 fewer deaths per 1000 treated.
ISIS-2.guideline_impact: Established aspirin as a permanent Class I recommendation in ACS in ACC/AHA and ESC guidelines.
ISIS-2.expert_takeaway: ACC Cardiology Hall of Fame cites ISIS-2 as the trial that proved a cheap pill could rival reperfusion in saving lives.

4S.primary_finding: Simvastatin reduced all-cause mortality 30% (11.5% vs 8.2%; ARR 3.3%, NNT 30) over 5.4 years.
4S.population: n=4,444 patients with prior MI/angina and total cholesterol 5.5-8.0 mmol/L.
4S.critique: Enrolled mostly middle-aged men with high baseline cholesterol; only 19% women; no diabetic or elderly subgroup powered.
4S.followup: 10-year follow-up (Lancet 2004) showed sustained 15% mortality reduction with no excess cancer.
4S.guideline_impact: First trial to make statins a Class I recommendation for secondary prevention in NCEP ATP-II/III and ESC dyslipidemia guidelines.
4S.expert_takeaway: ACC dubbed 4S the trial that ended the 'cholesterol controversy' and launched the statin era.

CARE.primary_finding: Pravastatin reduced fatal CHD or nonfatal MI by 24% (13.2% vs 10.2%; ARR 3%, NNT 33) over 5 years.
CARE.population: n=4,159 post-MI patients with average cholesterol (<240 mg/dL, mean LDL 139 mg/dL).
CARE.critique: No benefit when baseline LDL <125 mg/dL, raising concern of a 'floor effect'; unexpected breast cancer signal in women later unconfirmed.
CARE.followup: Pooled CARE/LIPID/WOSCOPS analyses confirmed benefit extended to lower LDL strata.
CARE.guideline_impact: Extended NCEP/AHA statin recommendations to post-MI patients without overt hypercholesterolemia.

HPS.primary_finding: Simvastatin 40 mg reduced major vascular events 24% (25.2% vs 19.8%; ARR 5.4%, NNT 19) over 5 years.
HPS.population: n=20,536 UK adults aged 40-80 with vascular disease or diabetes, any baseline LDL.
HPS.critique: Used fixed 40 mg dose; only ~25% of eligible UK patients enrolled, raising selection concerns; modest LDL reductions (~38 mg/dL).
HPS.followup: 11-year follow-up (Lancet 2011) showed persistent benefit with no late hazards.
HPS.guideline_impact: Drove ACC/AHA and ESC to recommend statins for diabetics and high-risk patients regardless of baseline LDL.
HPS.expert_takeaway: ACC Clinical Trials review called HPS the trial that severed statin benefit from baseline LDL level.

JUPITER.primary_finding: Rosuvastatin reduced primary CV endpoint 44% (HR 0.56; ARR 1.2%, NNT 95 over 1.9 years) in low-LDL/high-CRP adults.
JUPITER.population: n=17,802 adults LDL <130 mg/dL and hsCRP >=2.0 mg/L, no known CVD.
JUPITER.critique: Stopped early at 1.9 years; absolute event rates low; new-onset diabetes increased 27%; criticized for industry funding and CRP threshold.
JUPITER.followup: Subgroup analyses confirmed benefit even at LDL <50 mg/dL; CRP-guided strategy never formally adopted.
JUPITER.guideline_impact: Prompted 2013 ACC/AHA inclusion of hsCRP as risk-enhancing factor and broadened primary prevention statin indications.
JUPITER.expert_takeaway: JACC editorial (Hlatky 2008) cautioned the modest absolute benefit didn't justify universal CRP screening.

IMPROVE-IT.primary_finding: Ezetimibe+simvastatin reduced composite CV events 6.4% relatively (34.7% vs 32.7%; ARR 2.0%, NNT 50) over 6 years.
IMPROVE-IT.population: n=18,144 post-ACS patients with LDL 50-100 mg/dL on simvastatin background.
IMPROVE-IT.critique: Modest 2% absolute benefit; required 7-year follow-up to reach significance; no mortality reduction; simvastatin (not high-intensity) as comparator.
IMPROVE-IT.followup: Total-event analyses (JACC 2016) showed 9% reduction in recurrent events, strengthening benefit.
IMPROVE-IT.guideline_impact: 2018 ACC/AHA lipid guideline added ezetimibe as Class IIa add-on when LDL >=70 mg/dL on max statin in very-high-risk ASCVD.
IMPROVE-IT.expert_takeaway: ACC's Cannon called IMPROVE-IT the trial that confirmed 'LDL hypothesis' applies beyond statins.

FOURIER.primary_finding: Evolocumab reduced primary composite 15% (HR 0.85; 9.8% vs 11.3%; ARR 1.5%, NNT 67) at median 2.2 years; LDL median 30 mg/dL.
FOURIER.population: n=27,564 ASCVD patients on statin with LDL >=70 mg/dL.
FOURIER.critique: No cardiovascular or all-cause mortality benefit; short follow-up; cost-effectiveness widely questioned; 2022 reanalysis alleged miscounted deaths.
FOURIER.followup: FOURIER-OLE (Circulation 2022) showed continued reduction in CV death/MI/stroke over 5 additional years of open-label evolocumab.
FOURIER.guideline_impact: 2018 ACC/AHA cholesterol guidelines added PCSK9 inhibitors as Class IIa for very-high-risk ASCVD with LDL >=70 mg/dL despite max statin/ezetimibe.
FOURIER.expert_takeaway: JACC editorial (Stone/Lloyd-Jones) called FOURIER definitive proof 'lower LDL is better' without safety floor.

ODYSSEY OUTCOMES.primary_finding: Alirocumab reduced MACE 15% (HR 0.85; 9.5% vs 11.1%; ARR 1.6%, NNT 63) at median 2.8 years post-ACS.
ODYSSEY OUTCOMES.population: n=18,924 patients 1-12 months post-ACS with LDL >=70 mg/dL on high-intensity statin.
ODYSSEY OUTCOMES.critique: All-cause mortality benefit driven by post-hoc subgroup with LDL >=100 mg/dL; cost-effectiveness marginal at list price.
ODYSSEY OUTCOMES.followup: Long-term subanalyses showed durable benefit in polyvascular disease and prior MI subgroups.
ODYSSEY OUTCOMES.guideline_impact: Supported 2018 ACC/AHA Class IIa recommendation for PCSK9 inhibitors in very-high-risk ASCVD; ESC 2019 endorsed post-ACS use.
ODYSSEY OUTCOMES.expert_takeaway: ACC's Schwartz emphasized mortality signal as first for the class, distinguishing it from FOURIER.

HOPE.primary_finding: Ramipril 10 mg reduced composite CV death/MI/stroke 22% (17.8% vs 14.0%; ARR 3.8%, NNT 26) over 5 years.
HOPE.population: n=9,297 high-risk patients >=55 years with vascular disease or diabetes plus one risk factor, EF >40%.
HOPE.critique: BP measured only at trough, possibly underestimating BP-lowering contribution; questioned whether benefit was BP-mediated rather than pleiotropic.
HOPE.followup: HOPE-TOO (Circulation 2005) extended open-label follow-up showed durable reduction in MI and new diabetes.
HOPE.guideline_impact: ACC/AHA and ESC added ACE inhibitors as Class I for stable CAD, diabetes with risk factors, and high-risk vascular disease.
HOPE.expert_takeaway: ACC Clinical Trials archive credits HOPE with establishing ACE inhibition as vasculoprotective beyond BP control.

ALLHAT.primary_finding: Chlorthalidone equivalent to amlodipine/lisinopril for primary CHD outcome; lisinopril had higher combined CVD (33.3% vs 30.9%) and heart failure (8.7% vs 7.7%).
ALLHAT.population: n=33,357 hypertensive patients >=55 years with >=1 additional CHD risk factor.
ALLHAT.critique: Lisinopril arm disadvantaged in Black patients and by lack of permitted add-on diuretic; doxazosin arm stopped early for heart failure excess.
ALLHAT.followup: ALLHAT-LLT extension (2017) confirmed durability; subgroup analyses by race informed JNC 8 differential recommendations.
ALLHAT.guideline_impact: JNC 7 and JNC 8 endorsed thiazide-type diuretics as first-line antihypertensive; influenced ACC/AHA 2017 BP guideline.
ALLHAT.expert_takeaway: ACC's Furberg defended ALLHAT as proof that 'older, cheaper diuretics remain unsurpassed' for initial therapy.

CONSENSUS.primary_finding: Enalapril reduced 6-mo mortality 40% vs placebo (26% vs 44%) and 1-yr mortality 31% in NYHA IV HF; NNT ~6 at 6 months.
CONSENSUS.population: n=253 patients with severe (NYHA IV) congestive heart failure on digoxin/diuretics, randomized to enalapril vs placebo.
CONSENSUS.critique: Small trial limited to NYHA IV; no beta-blocker background (pre-modern GDMT); high early mortality made benefit easy to detect but generalizability narrow.
CONSENSUS.followup: 10-year follow-up (Eur Heart J 1999) showed sustained mortality benefit with 30% relative reduction maintained.
CONSENSUS.guideline_impact: Established ACE inhibitors as Class I therapy for symptomatic HFrEF in all subsequent AHA/ACC/ESC HF guidelines.

SOLVD.primary_finding: Enalapril reduced all-cause mortality 16% (35.2% vs 39.7%, p=0.0036) and HF hospitalization 26% over mean 41 months; NNT ~22 for mortality.
SOLVD.population: n=2,569 patients with EF <=35% and symptomatic HF (mostly NYHA II-III) on conventional therapy, randomized to enalapril vs placebo.
SOLVD.critique: Pre-beta-blocker era; ischemic etiology predominant (~70%) limiting applicability to nonischemic CM; modest absolute benefit in less-sick patients vs CONSENSUS.
SOLVD.followup: X-SOLVD extended follow-up (Circulation 2003) confirmed durable mortality benefit out to 12 years.
SOLVD.guideline_impact: Extended ACEi Class I indication to all symptomatic HFrEF (NYHA II-IV), and via SOLVD-Prevention arm to asymptomatic LV dysfunction.

MERIT-HF.primary_finding: Metoprolol succinate reduced all-cause mortality 34% (7.2% vs 11.0%/yr, p=0.00009) and sudden death 41%; trial stopped early; NNT ~26/year.
MERIT-HF.population: n=3,991 patients with NYHA II-IV HF, EF <=40%, on optimal background therapy.
MERIT-HF.critique: Underrepresented NYHA IV (only 4%); US subgroup showed nonsignificant mortality trend, raising concern about generalizability to sicker American patients.
MERIT-HF.followup: Subgroup analyses (JAMA 2000) confirmed benefit across age, sex, EF, and etiology; effect consistent regardless of baseline heart rate.
MERIT-HF.guideline_impact: Cemented beta-blockers (metoprolol succinate, carvedilol, bisoprolol) as Class I therapy for all stable HFrEF.

COPERNICUS.primary_finding: Carvedilol reduced all-cause mortality 35% (11.4% vs 18.5%, p=0.00013) in severe HF; trial stopped early for benefit; NNT ~14 at 10.4 months.
COPERNICUS.population: n=2,289 patients with severe HF (EF <25%, symptoms at rest or minimal exertion), euvolemic, on ACEi + diuretic.
COPERNICUS.critique: Excluded recently decompensated/IV inotrope patients and those needing ICU care, leaving question of safety in true acute decompensation unanswered.
COPERNICUS.followup: Pre-discharge initiation substudies (Krum, JAMA 2003) showed safety and benefit when started before hospital discharge.
COPERNICUS.guideline_impact: Extended beta-blocker Class I recommendation to severe (NYHA IIIb-IV) HFrEF, dispelling prior contraindication.

EMPHASIS-HF.primary_finding: Eplerenone reduced CV death/HF hospitalization 37% (18.3% vs 25.9%, HR 0.63) and all-cause mortality 24% in mild HF; NNT ~19 over 21 months.
EMPHASIS-HF.population: n=2,737 patients with NYHA II HF, EF <=35%, age >=55, on ACEi/ARB + beta-blocker; required recent CV hospitalization or elevated BNP.
EMPHASIS-HF.critique: Hyperkalemia (>5.5) doubled (11.8% vs 7.2%); enriched enrollment may overestimate benefit in stable outpatients.
EMPHASIS-HF.followup: Pooled MRA analyses and EPHESUS extension confirmed mortality benefit; real-world registries show persistent underuse and higher hyperkalemia rates.
EMPHASIS-HF.guideline_impact: Extended MRA Class I recommendation from NYHA III-IV (RALES) to NYHA II HFrEF in 2013 ACCF/AHA and 2012 ESC HF guidelines.

RACE II.primary_finding: Lenient rate control (HR <110) noninferior to strict (HR <80) for CV death/hospitalization/stroke at 3 years (12.9% vs 14.9%, HR 0.84, p<0.001 noninferiority).
RACE II.population: n=614 patients with permanent AFib <12 months, age <80, randomized to lenient vs strict rate-control strategy.
RACE II.critique: Underpowered for hard endpoints; permanent AFib only (not paroxysmal); short follow-up may miss tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy in lenient arm.
RACE II.followup: RACE II 3-year extension confirmed no difference in symptoms, QoL, or LV function between strategies.
RACE II.guideline_impact: 2014 AHA/ACC/HRS and 2016 ESC AFib guidelines endorsed lenient rate control (resting HR <110) as initial strategy for asymptomatic patients with preserved LV function.

RE-LY.primary_finding: Dabigatran 150mg reduced stroke/systemic embolism 35% vs warfarin (1.11% vs 1.69%/yr, p<0.001 superiority); 110mg noninferior; both reduced hemorrhagic stroke ~70%.
RE-LY.population: n=18,113 patients with nonvalvular AFib and >=1 stroke risk factor, randomized to dabigatran 110mg, 150mg, or warfarin (open-label).
RE-LY.critique: Open-label design (warfarin unblinded); mean TTR only 64%; higher GI bleeding with 150mg dose; MI signal (HR 1.38, p=0.048) raised concern.
RE-LY.followup: RELY-ABLE 2.3-year extension (Circulation 2013) confirmed sustained efficacy; meta-analyses found no significant MI excess.
RE-LY.guideline_impact: First DOAC approved for AFib; 2014 AHA/ACC/HRS guidelines added dabigatran as Class I alternative to warfarin for nonvalvular AFib.

ARISTOTLE.primary_finding: Apixaban reduced stroke/SE 21% (1.27% vs 1.60%/yr, p=0.01), major bleeding 31%, and all-cause mortality 11% vs warfarin; NNT 303/yr for stroke.
ARISTOTLE.population: n=18,201 patients with nonvalvular AFib and >=1 stroke risk factor (mean CHADS2 2.1), randomized to apixaban 5mg BID vs dose-adjusted warfarin.
ARISTOTLE.critique: Mean TTR 62% lower than ideal; relatively low-risk population (CHADS2 ~2); limited representation of very elderly (>80) and severe CKD patients.
ARISTOTLE.followup: Post-hoc analyses confirmed benefit across CHA2DS2-VASc strata and frailty; real-world ARISTOPHANES study replicated findings.
ARISTOTLE.guideline_impact: Apixaban became preferred DOAC in 2019 AHA/ACC/HRS focused update given best efficacy/safety profile; Class I for nonvalvular AFib.

ROCKET AF.primary_finding: Rivaroxaban noninferior to warfarin for stroke/SE (1.7% vs 2.2%/yr, HR 0.88, p<0.001 noninferiority); similar major bleeding; fewer ICH (0.5% vs 0.7%).
ROCKET AF.population: n=14,264 patients with nonvalvular AFib at moderate-high stroke risk (mean CHADS2 3.5), randomized to rivaroxaban 20mg daily vs warfarin.
ROCKET AF.critique: Warfarin TTR only 55% (lowest among DOAC trials); INR device recall raised concerns about warfarin arm management; higher-risk population than other DOAC trials.
ROCKET AF.followup: XANTUS and real-world registries confirmed effectiveness; subgroup analyses showed consistent benefit across renal function and age strata.
ROCKET AF.guideline_impact: Approved as alternative to warfarin in 2014 AHA/ACC/HRS AFib guidelines; Class I for nonvalvular AFib with moderate-high stroke risk.

ENGAGE AF.primary_finding: Edoxaban 60mg noninferior to warfarin for stroke/SE (1.18% vs 1.50%/yr, HR 0.79); 20% less major bleeding; 30mg dose had higher ischemic stroke.
ENGAGE AF.population: n=21,105 patients with nonvalvular AFib, CHADS2 >=2, randomized to edoxaban 60mg, 30mg, or warfarin; dose halved for CrCl 30-50, weight <=60kg, or P-gp inhibitors.
ENGAGE AF.critique: FDA noted reduced efficacy in patients with normal renal function (CrCl >95); 30mg dose inferior for stroke prevention; not approved in patients with preserved renal function.
ENGAGE AF.followup: Subgroup analyses confirmed benefit across age, renal function (CrCl 30-95), and prior VKA use; supported edoxaban use in elderly.
ENGAGE AF.guideline_impact: Added to 2019 AHA/ACC/HRS focused update as Class I DOAC option for nonvalvular AFib with CrCl 15-95 mL/min.

CABANA.primary_finding: Ablation did not reduce composite of death/disabling stroke/serious bleeding/cardiac arrest vs drug therapy (8.0% vs 9.2%, HR 0.86, p=0.30) in ITT analysis.
CABANA.population: n=2,204 patients with new-onset or undertreated AFib, age >=65 or <65 with >=1 stroke risk factor, randomized to catheter ablation vs rate/rhythm drugs.
CABANA.critique: 27.5% crossover from drug to ablation arm diluted ITT effect; per-protocol and as-treated analyses showed significant benefit; underpowered after event-rate reduction.
CABANA.followup: CABANA QoL substudy (JAMA 2019) showed significant improvement in AF-specific QoL with ablation; CASTLE-AF replicated mortality benefit in HF subgroup.
CABANA.guideline_impact: 2019 AHA/ACC/HRS focused update upgraded ablation to Class IIa for symptomatic AFib refractory to antiarrhythmics; Class IIb as first-line.
CABANA.expert_takeaway: ACC commentary: CABANA showed ablation is at least as good as drugs; per-protocol analysis and the HF subgroup (CASTLE-AF replication) make a strong case for ablation in selected patients.

COURAGE.primary_finding: PCI + OMT did not reduce death/MI vs OMT alone in stable CAD (19.0% vs 18.5% at 4.6 yrs, HR 1.05, p=0.62); PCI provided faster but not durable angina relief.
COURAGE.population: n=2,287 patients with stable angina, >=70% stenosis in >=1 vessel with objective ischemia, randomized to PCI + OMT vs OMT alone; predominantly bare-metal stents.
COURAGE.critique: Used predominantly bare-metal stents (pre-DES era); 32% crossover from OMT to PCI; excluded left main and severe symptoms; FFR-guided PCI not used.
COURAGE.followup: COURAGE 15-year extended follow-up (NEJM 2015) confirmed no mortality difference; ISCHEMIA trial (2020) reinforced findings with modern PCI and broader ischemia.
COURAGE.guideline_impact: 2012 ACC/AHA stable IHD guideline endorsed OMT as initial strategy for stable CAD; PCI reserved for refractory symptoms or high-risk anatomy.
COURAGE.expert_takeaway: CardioNerds/ACC: COURAGE changed the conversation from 'open the artery' to 'treat the patient'; OMT first, PCI for symptoms not prognosis in stable CAD.

COMPASS.primary_finding: Rivaroxaban 2.5mg BID + aspirin reduced CV death/stroke/MI 24% vs aspirin alone (4.1% vs 5.4%, HR 0.76, p<0.001); major bleeding increased (3.1% vs 1.9%); net benefit favored combination.
COMPASS.population: n=27,395 patients with stable atherosclerotic disease (CAD or PAD), randomized to rivaroxaban 2.5mg BID + ASA, rivaroxaban 5mg BID alone, or ASA alone.
COMPASS.critique: Trial stopped early for efficacy (mean follow-up 23 months) may overestimate benefit; excluded high bleeding risk patients; absolute risk reduction modest (1.3%).
COMPASS.followup: COMPASS PAD substudy showed benefit specifically in PAD patients; VOYAGER PAD extended findings to post-revascularization PAD setting.
COMPASS.guideline_impact: 2019 ESC chronic coronary syndrome guidelines and 2021 ACC/AHA chest pain guidelines added low-dose rivaroxaban + aspirin as Class IIa option for high-ischemic-risk stable CAD/PAD.
COMPASS.expert_takeaway: ACC: COMPASS established 'dual pathway inhibition' as a new strategy for high-risk stable atherosclerosis — modest absolute benefit but consistent across CAD and PAD.

DCCT.primary_finding: Intensive insulin (HbA1c 7.2% vs 9.0%) reduced retinopathy progression 54%, microalbuminuria 39%, neuropathy 60%; 3-fold higher severe hypoglycemia.
DCCT.population: n=1,441 T1DM patients age 13-39, baseline 1-15yr disease duration, followed mean 6.5 years.
DCCT.critique: Excluded patients >39yo, CV-disease, advanced complications; couldn't power CV endpoints due to young cohort.
DCCT.followup: EDIC (NEJM 2005) showed legacy effect: 57% reduction in nonfatal MI/stroke/CV death at 17yr despite HbA1c convergence.
DCCT.guideline_impact: ADA adopted HbA1c <7% target for T1DM and established intensive therapy as standard of care for all T1DM.
DCCT.expert_takeaway: Defined 'metabolic memory' — early tight control pays dividends decades later.

UKPDS 34.primary_finding: Metformin reduced any diabetes-related endpoint 32% (NNT~14), all-cause mortality 36%, MI 39% vs diet alone over 10.7yr.
UKPDS 34.population: n=1,704 newly diagnosed overweight (>120% IBW) T2DM patients, mean age 53, randomized to metformin vs diet vs sulfonylurea/insulin.
UKPDS 34.critique: Small metformin arm (n=342), unexplained excess mortality when metformin added to sulfonylurea subgroup.
UKPDS 34.followup: UKPDS 10-year post-trial follow-up (NEJM 2008) confirmed sustained 33% MI and 27% mortality reduction despite glycemic convergence.
UKPDS 34.guideline_impact: Established metformin as first-line T2DM therapy in ADA/EASD guidelines, position retained through 2026.
UKPDS 34.expert_takeaway: Drug-specific benefit beyond glucose lowering — likely the most important T2DM trial ever conducted.

ADVANCE.primary_finding: Intensive control (HbA1c 6.5% vs 7.3%) reduced combined macro/microvascular events 10% (HR 0.90), driven entirely by 21% nephropathy reduction; no CV benefit.
ADVANCE.population: n=11,140 T2DM patients with CV risk factors or established disease, mean age 66, randomized to gliclazide-based intensive vs standard.
ADVANCE.critique: Lower hypoglycemia/mortality vs ACCORD suggested gradual A1c lowering was safer than aggressive titration.
ADVANCE.followup: ADVANCE-ON (NEJM 2014) found no legacy benefit on CV/mortality at 5.4yr post-trial, but persistent renal benefit.
ADVANCE.guideline_impact: ADA shifted toward individualized A1c targets, tempering universal <7% recommendation post-ACCORD/ADVANCE/VADT.

VADT.primary_finding: Intensive control (HbA1c 6.9% vs 8.4%) showed no significant CV benefit (HR 0.88, p=0.14) over 5.6yr; doubled severe hypoglycemia.
VADT.population: n=1,791 mostly male veterans with poorly controlled T2DM (baseline A1c 9.4%), mean age 60, 40% with prior CV event.
VADT.critique: Advanced disease duration (~11.5yr) and existing complications limited capacity for benefit — too late to intervene.
VADT.followup: VADT 10-year follow-up (NEJM 2015) found modest CV benefit (HR 0.83) emerging late; 15-year (NEJM 2019) showed benefit lost.
VADT.guideline_impact: Reinforced ADA's individualized targets — less stringent A1c (~8%) acceptable in elderly with long-standing disease and comorbidities.

LEADER.primary_finding: Liraglutide reduced 3-point MACE 13% (13.0% vs 14.9%, HR 0.87, NNT=53), CV death 22%, all-cause mortality 15% over 3.8yr.
LEADER.population: n=9,340 T2DM with established CVD (81%) or high CV risk, mean age 64, baseline A1c 8.7%.
LEADER.critique: Modest absolute benefit (1.9%); unclear mechanism beyond glycemia/weight; exclusion of younger primary-prevention patients.
LEADER.followup: Pooled GLP-1 meta-analyses (Lancet D&E 2021) confirmed class effect; LEADER renal substudy showed 22% reduction in nephropathy.
LEADER.guideline_impact: ADA elevated GLP-1 RAs to preferred second-line after metformin for T2DM with established ASCVD (2018 update).
LEADER.expert_takeaway: First GLP-1 RA to show definitive CV mortality benefit, opening the era of outcome-driven T2DM therapy.

SUSTAIN-6.primary_finding: Semaglutide reduced MACE 26% (6.6% vs 8.9%, HR 0.74, NNT=44), driven by 39% nonfatal stroke reduction; increased retinopathy complications (HR 1.76).
SUSTAIN-6.population: n=3,297 T2DM with CVD/CKD/high CV risk, mean age 65, randomized to weekly semaglutide vs placebo for 104 weeks.
SUSTAIN-6.critique: Pre-marketing non-inferiority (underpowered for superiority); retinopathy signal unexplained and worrying.
SUSTAIN-6.followup: PIONEER 6 (oral semaglutide, NEJM 2019) confirmed CV safety; SELECT (NEJM 2023) showed MACE benefit in non-diabetic obesity.
SUSTAIN-6.guideline_impact: Contributed to ADA preferred GLP-1 RA designation; FDA approved semaglutide CV indication in 2020.

REWIND.primary_finding: Dulaglutide reduced MACE 12% (12.0% vs 13.4%, HR 0.88, NNT=60) over 5.4yr — longest GLP-1 CVOT.
REWIND.population: n=9,901 T2DM, only 31% with established CVD (majority primary prevention), mean age 66, baseline A1c 7.2%.
REWIND.critique: Modest absolute risk reduction over 5+ years; whether benefit extends to truly low-risk primary-prevention patients remains uncertain.
REWIND.followup: Subgroup analysis (Lancet 2019) confirmed consistent benefit regardless of prior CVD; cognitive substudy showed reduced cognitive decline.
REWIND.guideline_impact: Expanded ADA recommendation for GLP-1 RA to T2DM with multiple CV risk factors, not just established ASCVD.
REWIND.expert_takeaway: First CVOT to demonstrate benefit predominantly in primary prevention population.

DECLARE-TIMI 58.primary_finding: Dapagliflozin did not reduce MACE (HR 0.93, p=0.17) but reduced CV death/HF hospitalization 17% (HR 0.83, NNT=125) over 4.2yr.
DECLARE-TIMI 58.population: n=17,160 T2DM, 40% with established ASCVD, 60% with multiple risk factors, baseline A1c 8.3%.
DECLARE-TIMI 58.critique: Failure of MACE primary endpoint; HF benefit driven by hospitalization (subjective), not CV death.
DECLARE-TIMI 58.followup: DAPA-HF (NEJM 2019) confirmed HF benefit independent of diabetes; DAPA-CKD (NEJM 2020) extended to kidney outcomes.
DECLARE-TIMI 58.guideline_impact: ADA/ACC now recommend SGLT2 inhibitors for T2DM with HF or CKD regardless of glycemic control.
DECLARE-TIMI 58.expert_takeaway: Reframed SGLT2 inhibitors as primarily cardiorenal — not glucose — drugs.

SURMOUNT-1.primary_finding: Tirzepatide 15mg achieved 20.9% mean weight loss vs 3.1% placebo at 72wk; 91% achieved >=5% loss (NNT~1.1).
SURMOUNT-1.population: n=2,539 adults with obesity (BMI>=30) or BMI>=27 with comorbidity, without diabetes, mean BMI 38.
SURMOUNT-1.critique: Absent long-term CV/mortality data; history of obesity drugs (fen-phen, lorcaserin) later withdrawn.
SURMOUNT-1.followup: SURMOUNT-4 (JAMA 2024) showed regain after discontinuation; SURMOUNT-MMO (2026) cardiovascular outcomes trial pending.
SURMOUNT-1.guideline_impact: Led to FDA approval of tirzepatide for obesity (Zepbound, 2023); AACE 2024 endorsed as preferred pharmacotherapy.
SURMOUNT-1.expert_takeaway: Bariatric-surgery-level weight loss from an injection — but durability and CV outcomes still unproven.

CHECKMATE 067.primary_finding: Nivo+ipi median PFS 11.5mo vs nivo 6.9mo vs ipi 2.9mo; 10-year OS 43% (combo) vs 37% (nivo) vs 19% (ipi).
CHECKMATE 067.population: n=945 previously untreated unresectable stage III/IV melanoma, randomized 1:1:1 to nivo+ipi, nivo, or ipi.
CHECKMATE 067.critique: Combo's 55% grade 3-4 toxicity; lack of direct nivo+ipi vs nivo statistical comparison in initial design.
CHECKMATE 067.followup: 10-year follow-up (NEJM 2025) confirmed durable plateau in OS curves, with median OS 71.9mo (combo) vs 36.9mo (nivo) vs 19.9mo (ipi).
CHECKMATE 067.guideline_impact: NCCN designated nivo+ipi category 1 first-line for advanced melanoma; established dual checkpoint blockade paradigm.
CHECKMATE 067.expert_takeaway: Transformed metastatic melanoma from uniformly fatal to potentially curable for ~40% of patients.

KEYNOTE-024.primary_finding: Pembrolizumab improved median PFS 10.3mo vs 6.0mo (HR 0.50), 5-year OS 31.9% vs 16.3% despite 66% crossover.
KEYNOTE-024.population: n=305 untreated stage IV NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS >=50%, no EGFR/ALK alterations.
KEYNOTE-024.critique: Exclusion of EGFR/ALK and PD-L1<50% patients (~70% of NSCLC), limiting generalizability.
KEYNOTE-024.followup: 5-year update (JCO 2021, Brahmer) confirmed sustained benefit; KEYNOTE-042 extended to PD-L1>=1% with attenuated benefit.
KEYNOTE-024.guideline_impact: NCCN established pembrolizumab monotherapy as preferred first-line for PD-L1>=50% advanced NSCLC; mandated PD-L1 testing.
KEYNOTE-024.expert_takeaway: Made chemo-free first-line therapy the standard for high PD-L1 NSCLC.

CLL14.primary_finding: Fixed 12-mo venetoclax+obinutuzumab improved 2-yr PFS 88% vs 64% (HR 0.35, NNT=4) vs chlorambucil+obinutuzumab; deeper MRD-negative responses.
CLL14.population: n=432 untreated CLL with comorbidities (CIRS>6 or CrCl<70), median age 72.
CLL14.critique: Chlorambucil-based comparator (already outdated by 2019); absence of head-to-head vs BTK inhibitors.
CLL14.followup: 6-year follow-up (Blood 2024, Al-Sawaf): sustained PFS benefit (53% vs 21.7%), TTNT 65%, supporting fixed-duration paradigm.
CLL14.guideline_impact: NCCN/iwCLL endorsed venetoclax+obinutuzumab as preferred fixed-duration first-line CLL therapy in 2020.
CLL14.expert_takeaway: Established chemo-free, time-limited therapy as new CLL standard, sparing patients indefinite BTK inhibitor exposure.

MAIA.primary_finding: Daratumumab+Rd reduced progression/death 44% (HR 0.56) vs Rd; 30-mo PFS 71% vs 56% (NNT=7); higher MRD-negativity (24% vs 7%).
MAIA.population: n=737 newly diagnosed transplant-ineligible multiple myeloma, median age 73.
MAIA.critique: Higher pneumonia/neutropenia rates; indefinite daratumumab duration (cost/burden); no OS benefit at primary analysis.
MAIA.followup: Final OS analysis (Lancet Oncol 2021) confirmed median OS not reached vs 65.5mo with Rd (HR 0.68); benefit sustained beyond 5 years.
MAIA.guideline_impact: NCCN designated D-Rd preferred first-line for transplant-ineligible MM; reshaped induction paradigm for elderly patients.
MAIA.expert_takeaway: Triplet therapy now expected standard even for frail/elderly MM patients.

ALCYONE.primary_finding: Daratumumab+VMP reduced progression/death 50% (HR 0.50); 18-mo PFS 71.6% vs 50.2% (NNT=5); doubled CR rate (43% vs 24%).
ALCYONE.population: n=706 newly diagnosed transplant-ineligible multiple myeloma, median age 71.
ALCYONE.critique: VMP backbone (declining use in US in favor of Rd); 9-cycle bortezomib limit; peripheral neuropathy concern.
ALCYONE.followup: Final analysis (Lancet 2020) showed sustained OS benefit (HR 0.60, median OS not reached vs 53.6mo) at median 40.1mo.
ALCYONE.guideline_impact: Supported FDA approval of daratumumab in newly diagnosed transplant-ineligible MM (2018); NCCN added D-VMP as option.

ARDS Network.primary_finding: Conservative fluid strategy did not change 60-day mortality (25.5% vs 28.4%, p=0.30) but improved ventilator-free days (14.6 vs 12.1, p<0.001).
ARDS Network.population: n=1000 adults with acute lung injury/ARDS on mechanical ventilation without shock, randomized within 48h of intubation.
ARDS Network.critique: Excluded patients in shock; near-zero net fluid balance hard to replicate; protocol complex and rarely operationalized at bedside.
ARDS Network.followup: Long-term cognitive follow-up suggested conservative arm had more cognitive impairment at 12 months.
ARDS Network.guideline_impact: ATS/ESICM/SCCM ARDS guidelines recommend conservative fluid strategy in ARDS without shock after initial resuscitation.
ARDS Network.expert_takeaway: PulmCrit: dry lungs are happy lungs, but only after resuscitation; aim for even fluid balance, not aggressive diuresis in shock.

EOLIA.primary_finding: VV-ECMO did not significantly reduce 60-day mortality vs conventional ventilation (35% vs 46%, RR 0.76, p=0.09); 28% crossover to rescue ECMO.
EOLIA.population: n=249 adults with very severe ARDS (P/F<50 for 3h, <80 for 6h, or pH<7.25 with PaCO2>=60).
EOLIA.critique: Stopped early for futility despite trend; high crossover diluted effect; post-hoc Bayesian analysis showed >96% probability of benefit.
EOLIA.followup: 2018 Bayesian reanalysis and 2020 IPD meta-analysis with CESAR showed significant mortality benefit of ECMO.
EOLIA.guideline_impact: ELSO and ATS 2023 guidelines recommend ECMO referral for severe ARDS meeting EOLIA criteria at experienced centers.
EOLIA.expert_takeaway: PulmCrit (Farkas): EOLIA is a positive trial mislabeled negative; Bayesian framing reveals near-certain benefit in selected patients.

CESAR.primary_finding: Referral to ECMO center reduced death or severe disability at 6 months (37% vs 53%, RR 0.69, p=0.03; NNT 6).
CESAR.population: n=180 UK adults aged 18-65 with severe but reversible respiratory failure (Murray>3.0 or pH<7.20).
CESAR.critique: Pragmatic trial of referral not ECMO itself; 24% of referred patients never received ECMO; control arm lacked standardized lung-protective ventilation.
CESAR.followup: Long-term UK cost-effectiveness analysis supported ECMO referral; informed H1N1 ECMO triage in 2009 pandemic.
CESAR.guideline_impact: Established ECMO referral pathway for severe ARDS in UK and influenced ELSO international referral criteria.
CESAR.expert_takeaway: REBEL EM: tests a system not a device; benefit may reflect protocolized care at ECMO centers as much as ECMO itself.

ADRENAL.primary_finding: Hydrocortisone did not reduce 90-day mortality vs placebo in septic shock (27.9% vs 28.8%, OR 0.95, p=0.50) but faster shock resolution (3 vs 4 days).
ADRENAL.population: n=3800 adults with septic shock requiring vasopressors and mechanical ventilation across 69 ICUs in 5 countries.
