ADRENAL.critique: Lower baseline severity than APROCCHSS (mortality ~28% vs 49%); no fludrocortisone; bolus dosing in APROCCHSS may have differed pharmacodynamically.
ADRENAL.followup: 2020 6-month follow-up confirmed no mortality benefit; 2023 individual patient meta-analysis showed modest mortality benefit pooled across trials.
ADRENAL.guideline_impact: SSC 2021 weakly recommends hydrocortisone in septic shock with ongoing vasopressor requirement, citing ADRENAL+APROCCHSS together.
ADRENAL.expert_takeaway: REBEL EM: steroids speed shock resolution but don't save lives; reasonable in refractory shock, not mandatory.

APROCCHSS.primary_finding: Hydrocortisone+fludrocortisone reduced 90-day mortality vs placebo (43.0% vs 49.1%, RR 0.88, p=0.03; NNT 17).
APROCCHSS.population: n=1241 French adults with septic shock for >=6h on vasopressors with SOFA>=3 in >=2 organs.
APROCCHSS.critique: Sicker cohort than ADRENAL; protocol switched mid-trial after drotrecogin withdrawal; bolus hydrocortisone plus enteral fludrocortisone hard to compare across studies.
APROCCHSS.followup: 2024 Lancet Respiratory subgroup analysis showed largest benefit in community-acquired pneumonia septic shock.
APROCCHSS.guideline_impact: SSC 2021 supports hydrocortisone in septic shock; debate continues over adding fludrocortisone.
APROCCHSS.expert_takeaway: PulmCrit: fludrocortisone is the secret sauce; consider adding 50 mcg daily to hydrocortisone in refractory shock.

VASST.primary_finding: Low-dose vasopressin vs norepinephrine did not reduce 28-day mortality in septic shock (35.4% vs 39.3%, RR 0.90, p=0.26).
VASST.population: n=778 adults with septic shock on >=5 mcg/min norepinephrine equivalents across 27 ICUs.
VASST.critique: Underpowered; subgroup of less-severe shock (NE 5-15 mcg/min) showed mortality benefit driving guideline use; open-label catecholamine titration.
VASST.followup: VANISH (2016) showed no mortality benefit of vasopressin-first vs norepinephrine-first but less AKI requiring RRT.
VASST.guideline_impact: SSC 2021 recommends adding vasopressin to norepinephrine when MAP target unmet, citing VASST+VANISH.
VASST.expert_takeaway: EMCrit: vasopressin as second-line catecholamine-sparer is reasonable; routine first-line use not supported.

SMART.primary_finding: Balanced crystalloids reduced MAKE30 (death, RRT, persistent renal dysfunction) vs saline (14.3% vs 15.4%, OR 0.91, p=0.04; NNT 94).
SMART.population: n=15,802 critically ill adults in 5 Vanderbilt ICUs in cluster-crossover trial.
SMART.critique: Single-center, unblinded, cluster-crossover; small absolute difference; composite driven by death not RRT; baseline imbalances between months.
SMART.followup: 2019 sepsis subgroup analysis showed larger benefit in sepsis (33.8% vs 38.9% MAKE30); BaSICS and PLUS later showed no benefit.
SMART.guideline_impact: SSC 2021 weakly recommends balanced crystalloids over saline for resuscitation in sepsis.
SMART.expert_takeaway: PulmCrit: ditch saline by default; the signal across SMART+meta-analysis favors balanced even if individual mega-trials are null.

BaSICS.primary_finding: Balanced solution did not reduce 90-day mortality vs saline (26.4% vs 27.2%, HR 0.97, p=0.47) in critically ill patients.
BaSICS.population: n=10,520 ICU patients at 75 Brazilian ICUs with >=1 risk factor and expected >24h ICU stay; factorial with slow/fast infusion.
BaSICS.critique: Mostly elective surgical, low-severity patients with small fluid volumes (median ~1.5L); modest median exposure limited ability to detect difference.
BaSICS.followup: TBI subgroup post hoc showed potential harm with balanced solution; informed PLUS interpretation.
BaSICS.guideline_impact: Tempered SSC enthusiasm for balanced fluids; recommendations remain weak/conditional pending IPD meta-analyses.
BaSICS.expert_takeaway: First10EM: saline is fine in average ICU patients; balanced may still matter when large volumes are needed.

PLUS.primary_finding: Plasma-Lyte 148 did not reduce 90-day mortality vs saline (21.8% vs 22.0%, OR 0.99, p=0.90) or new RRT in ICU patients.
PLUS.population: n=5037 critically ill adults in 53 Australia/New Zealand ICUs expected to need fluid and >=48h ICU stay.
PLUS.critique: Median exposure only ~3.9L; high pre-randomization fluid exposure may have diluted effect; lower-severity than expected.
PLUS.followup: 2022 PLUS+BaSICS IPD meta-analysis with SMART suggested possible small benefit in sepsis but null overall.
PLUS.guideline_impact: SSC kept balanced crystalloids as weak recommendation; equipoise reopened for general ICU population.
PLUS.expert_takeaway: REBEL EM: in unselected ICU patients, fluid choice probably doesn't matter much; reserve balanced for large-volume sepsis resuscitation.

LOVIT.primary_finding: High-dose IV vitamin C increased 28-day death or persistent organ dysfunction vs placebo (44.5% vs 38.5%, RR 1.21, p=0.01; NNH 17).
LOVIT.population: n=872 ICU adults with sepsis on vasopressors, randomized within 24h of vasopressor start to vitamin C 50 mg/kg q6h x 96h vs placebo.
LOVIT.critique: Abrupt vitamin C cessation may have caused rebound oxidative stress; no metabolic cofactor co-administration; composite endpoint driven by mortality signal.
LOVIT.followup: 2022 secondary analysis suggested abrupt vitamin C withdrawal contributed to harm; LOVIT-COVID also null/harmful.
LOVIT.guideline_impact: SSC 2021 recommends against IV vitamin C in sepsis; effectively closed the Marik metabolic cocktail era.
LOVIT.expert_takeaway: PulmCrit (Farkas): vitamin C in sepsis is dead; LOVIT was the nail in the coffin after CITRIS-ALI and VICTAS.

PALISADE.primary_finding: 67% of AR101 vs 4% placebo tolerated 600mg peanut protein at exit challenge; ARR 63%, NNT 2 for desensitization.
PALISADE.population: n=496 peanut-allergic children/adolescents ages 4-17 reactive to <=100mg peanut protein at baseline.
PALISADE.critique: 14% required epinephrine during therapy; high withdrawal (~20%) from adverse events; desensitization, not tolerance.
PALISADE.followup: Chu PACE meta-analysis (Lancet 2019) showed OIT tripled anaphylaxis risk vs avoidance despite desensitization.
PALISADE.guideline_impact: FDA approved Palforzia (AR101) Jan 2020; AAAAI/EAACI cautiously endorse OIT in select pediatric patients in specialty centers.
PALISADE.expert_takeaway: Desensitization is real but trades bite-protection for more frequent reactions during build-up — informed shared decision essential.

OUtMATCH.primary_finding: 67% omalizumab vs 7% placebo tolerated >=600mg peanut without dose-limiting symptoms; ARR 60%, NNT ~2.
OUtMATCH.population: n=177 children/adults (1-55y) with peanut allergy plus >=2 other food allergies (cashew, milk, egg, walnut).
OUtMATCH.critique: No oral tolerance induced — requires continuous dosing; Stage 2 showed no benefit over OIT alone for sustained tolerance.
OUtMATCH.followup: Stage 2 (NEJM 2025) compared omalizumab-facilitated multi-allergen OIT vs OIT alone; longer-term real-world registries ongoing.
OUtMATCH.guideline_impact: FDA approved omalizumab (Xolair) Feb 2024 as first drug for IgE-mediated food allergy; AAAAI 2024 practice parameter incorporated.
OUtMATCH.expert_takeaway: Game-changer for multi-food allergic patients but requires indefinite injections — practical and cost barriers remain.

ION-1.primary_finding: SVR12 of 97-99% with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir +/-ribavirin for 12 or 24 weeks in treatment-naive HCV genotype 1; NNT ~2 vs historical IFN.
ION-1.population: n=865 previously untreated chronic HCV genotype 1 adults; 16% with compensated cirrhosis.
ION-1.critique: Gilead-sponsored, no active comparator; cirrhotic and Black subgroups underpowered; SVR12 not validated against clinical outcomes.
ION-1.followup: Real-world cohorts (HCV-TARGET, TRIO) confirmed >95% SVR; long-term registries show HCC risk reduced but not eliminated post-SVR.
ION-1.guideline_impact: AASLD/IDSA HCV guidance (2014->) made LDV/SOF first-line for genotype 1; interferon abandoned.
ION-1.expert_takeaway: Ushered in the interferon-free era — HCV became a curable disease in 12 weeks of oral therapy.

ASTRAL-1.primary_finding: SVR12 99% (618/624) with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir vs 0% placebo across HCV genotypes 1,2,4,5,6; NNT 1.
ASTRAL-1.population: n=740 chronic HCV genotypes 1,2,4,5,6 (including 19% cirrhotic, 32% treatment-experienced); randomized 5:1 to SOF/VEL vs placebo.
ASTRAL-1.critique: Placebo (not active) comparator — ethically unusual; genotype 3 evaluated separately in ASTRAL-3; limited decompensated cirrhosis data.
ASTRAL-1.followup: ASTRAL-4 (decompensated cirrhosis) and ASTRAL-5 (HIV coinfection) extended applicability; long-term SVR durability >99%.
ASTRAL-1.guideline_impact: AASLD/IDSA and EASL endorsed SOF/VEL (Epclusa) as pan-genotypic first-line; simplified pretreatment genotyping.
ASTRAL-1.expert_takeaway: Made genotype testing largely irrelevant — one pill, all genotypes, near-universal cure.

ACTT-1.primary_finding: Remdesivir shortened recovery from 15 to 10 days (RR 1.29, p<0.001); mortality 11.4% vs 15.2% (HR 0.73, NS); NNT for recovery ~5.
ACTT-1.population: n=1062 hospitalized adults with COVID-19 and lower respiratory tract involvement; double-blind, placebo-controlled.
ACTT-1.critique: Baseline imbalance favored remdesivir arm (more good-prognosis patients); no mortality benefit; primary endpoint changed mid-trial.
ACTT-1.followup: WHO Solidarity (Lancet 2022) and meta-analyses showed no mortality benefit overall; modest benefit possibly in non-ventilated oxygen-requiring patients.
ACTT-1.guideline_impact: FDA full approval Oct 2020; IDSA/NIH guidelines recommend in hospitalized patients needing supplemental but not invasive ventilation.
ACTT-1.expert_takeaway: Modest recovery benefit only — overshadowed by dexamethasone and IL-6 antagonists for sicker patients.

REMAP-CAP.primary_finding: Tocilizumab/sarilumab improved organ-support-free days (median 10 vs 0) and reduced in-hospital mortality 28% vs 36%; NNT ~12.
REMAP-CAP.population: n=803 critically ill COVID-19 adults within 24h of ICU organ support; Bayesian adaptive platform trial.
REMAP-CAP.critique: Open-label; concurrent steroid use evolved during enrollment confounding effect estimate; anakinra arm dropped for futility.
REMAP-CAP.followup: RECOVERY (Lancet 2021) confirmed tocilizumab mortality benefit in hospitalized hypoxic patients; meta-analyses support IL-6 blockade with steroids.
REMAP-CAP.guideline_impact: WHO, NIH, IDSA recommend tocilizumab (or sarilumab) added to steroids in rapidly progressing severe/critical COVID-19.
REMAP-CAP.expert_takeaway: Adaptive platform design itself became a model — demonstrated how to learn during a pandemic.

STOP-IgAN.primary_finding: Adding immunosuppression to supportive care did not reduce eGFR loss (no difference at 3y); full remission 17% vs 5% but no renal protection.
STOP-IgAN.population: n=162 adults with IgAN and persistent proteinuria >0.75g/d despite 6-month optimized supportive care run-in (RAS blockade).
STOP-IgAN.critique: Excluded eGFR<30; mostly Caucasian; short 3-year primary endpoint; underpowered for hard endpoints like ESKD.
STOP-IgAN.followup: 10-year follow-up (KI 2020) confirmed no benefit on death/ESKD/eGFR loss >40% (HR 1.20, 95% CI 0.75-1.92).
STOP-IgAN.guideline_impact: KDIGO 2021 IgAN guidelines downgraded routine corticosteroids; emphasized optimized supportive care first.
STOP-IgAN.expert_takeaway: Reframed IgAN management — optimize supportive care exhaustively before considering immunosuppression's harms.

TESTING.primary_finding: Methylprednisolone reduced composite kidney failure/eGFR decline/renal death by 47% (HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.39-0.72); NNT ~7 over 4.2y.
TESTING.population: n=503 adults with IgAN, proteinuria >=1g/d and eGFR 20-120 despite RAS blockade; ~75% Asian.
TESTING.critique: Original full-dose arm halted early for serious infections (8.1% vs 0%, including 2 deaths); reduced-dose arm safer but trial heterogeneous.
TESTING.followup: Reduced-dose extension (KI Reports 2024) confirmed efficacy with lower infection rate; long-term follow-up ongoing.
TESTING.guideline_impact: KDIGO 2024 update conditionally recommends reduced-dose steroids for high-risk IgAN after optimized supportive care, with infection prophylaxis.
TESTING.expert_takeaway: Steroids work in IgAN — but harm is real; weigh against newer agents (sparsentan, targeted-release budesonide).

ECASS-III.primary_finding: Alteplase 3-4.5h improved mRS 0-1 at 90 days 52.4% vs 45.2% (OR 1.34); ARR 7.2%, NNT 14; symptomatic ICH 2.4% vs 0.2%.
ECASS-III.population: n=821 adults with acute ischemic stroke 3-4.5h from onset; excluded NIHSS>25, prior stroke+diabetes, anticoagulation.
ECASS-III.critique: Baseline imbalance — placebo arm had higher NIHSS and more prior stroke; Alper 2020 reanalysis showed no significant benefit after adjustment.
ECASS-III.followup: IST-3 (Lancet 2012) and pooled Emberson meta-analysis (Lancet 2014) supported benefit up to 4.5h; benefit time-dependent.
ECASS-III.guideline_impact: AHA/ASA 2009->2019 guidelines extended tPA window to 4.5h for eligible patients; ESO follows similar.
ECASS-III.expert_takeaway: Time-window extension still debated by EM physicians — emphasizes 'time is brain' over absolute hour cutoff.

MR CLEAN.primary_finding: Endovascular thrombectomy +IV tPA improved functional independence (mRS 0-2) 32.6% vs 19.1%; ARR 13.5%, NNT 7; no mortality difference.
MR CLEAN.population: n=500 adults with acute ischemic stroke from proximal anterior circulation occlusion, treatable within 6h of onset.
MR CLEAN.critique: Only 1.4% used latest-generation stent retrievers initially; control group recovery rate lower than other contemporary trials.
MR CLEAN.followup: HERMES pooled analysis (Lancet 2016, n=1287) confirmed benefit across 5 trials (cOR 2.49); DAWN/DEFUSE-3 extended window to 24h.
MR CLEAN.guideline_impact: AHA/ASA 2015 emergency update made mechanical thrombectomy standard of care for LVO stroke; restructured stroke systems globally.
MR CLEAN.expert_takeaway: Single most impactful stroke trial of the decade — made stroke a true endovascular emergency.

TEMEL.primary_finding: Early palliative care improved QoL (FACT-L 98 vs 91.5, p=0.03), reduced depression, and extended median survival 11.6 vs 8.9mo (NNT ~7 for 1y survival).
TEMEL.population: n=151 adults with newly diagnosed metastatic NSCLC; single-center MGH; randomized within 8 weeks of diagnosis.
TEMEL.critique: Single-center, unblinded, predominantly white well-resourced cohort; less aggressive end-of-life care may confound survival.
TEMEL.followup: ENABLE III (JCO 2015) and Bakitas trials confirmed QoL/mood benefits; mortality benefit not consistently replicated across cancer types.
TEMEL.guideline_impact: ASCO 2012/2017/2024 guidelines recommend early palliative care concurrent with oncology care for advanced cancer within 8 weeks.
TEMEL.expert_takeaway: Counterintuitive but reproducible — less aggressive care may extend life; reframed palliative care from end-of-life to early integration.
